grounding.summary: The osf-archive/ working tree contains ONLY the 21 Phase 1 transcripts (p1s1.txt through p7s3.txt). All XLSX gold analyses, all IRR CSVs, kappa.Rmd/kappa.html, Phase 2 transcripts, and R scripts were removed in git commit 1bf235f ("chore: update plugin skills, remove osf-archive binaries, fix sync test") and exist only in git history at parent commit d99e9f5. They are fully recoverable via git show. The IRR data is for a SINGLE transcript: p3s1 (Participant 3, Suggestion 1, Scored 2/5 — a moderate-category transcript). Two human raters are Kevin Sheldrake ("kev") and a second analyst ("yesesvi"). The original authors measured Cohen's kappa using a hand-rolled formula (not sklearn) producing diachronic κ = 0.82 (strong agreement) and synchronic κ = 0.60 (moderate agreement). The Moment column in the diachronic CSVs IS the experienced-moment ordering signal: kev assigned 7 distinct moments (range 1–7), yesesvi assigned 6 distinct moments (range 1–6, with a recode of moment 6→7). Ordering information IS recoverable from the IRR CSVs: utterance→IDU assignment and utterance→Moment (experienced-order) assignment are both explicit. The human-human ordering-disagreement band can be computed from these two raters on p3s1. The XLSX gold analyses (per-transcript diachronic+synchronic+structure for p1s1–p7s3 in Phase 1, p8s1–p13s3 in Phase 2) contain full IDU tables with utterance-number lists, moment assignments, and diachronic structure — the data needed for Kendall tau vs gold. The runs/phase1 analyses are LLM-generated scratch (normalize_diachronic.py explicitly fabricates placeholder data for missing inputs) and must NOT be used as gold. The transcript format in osf-archive/ matches the plugin's expected header exactly: "Participant N, Suggestion N (Scored N/5)" followed by a blank line and then interleaved Kevin Sheldrake / P-speaker turns — but utterances are NOT pre-numbered; the plugin's transcript_prep step assigns utterance numbers. Phase 2 had 18 transcripts (p8–p13, 3 suggestions each). Total OSF dataset: 7 participants × 3 suggestions = 21 Phase 1 + 6 participants × 3 suggestions = 18 Phase 2 = 39 transcripts total. All OSF transcript content is recoverable from git history.
key_facts: osf-archive/ working tree: ONLY C:/microphenomenograph/osf-archive/Phase 1/transcripts/ with 21 .txt files (p1s1.txt through p7s3.txt). No XLSX, no CSV, no R scripts in working tree.

All OSF gold data removed in commit 1bf235f (2026-05-17): removed osf-archive/Inter-rater Reliability/ (9 files), osf-archive/Phase 1/analyses/ (21 XLSX + 4 aggregation XLSX), osf-archive/Phase 2/ (18 transcripts + 18 analyses XLSX + 4 aggregation XLSX), osf-archive/R/ (15 files including kappa.Rmd), osf-archive/*.pdf. Recoverable via: git show d99e9f5:<path>

IRR data covers EXACTLY ONE transcript: p3s1 (Participant 3, Suggestion 1, Scored 2/5, moderate IV category). This is the only transcript for which a human-human ordering-disagreement band can be computed from the available OSF data.

Two human raters in IRR CSVs: 'kev' (Kevin Sheldrake, primary analyst) in kev-diachronic-analysis.csv and kev-synchronic-analysis.csv; 'yesesvi' (independent second analyst) in yesesvi-diachronic-analysis.csv and yesesvi-synchronic-analysis.csv. Both files contain Speaker, #, Utterance, Moment, IDU, Criteria columns (diachronic) or IDU, #, Utterance, Criteria, ISU, ISU 2nd Level, ISUnum (synchronic).

kappa.Rmd (git: d99e9f5:osf-archive/Inter-rater Reliability/kappa.Rmd) confirms: Authors measured Cohen's kappa using a hand-rolled R formula (not sklearn/krippendorff). The formula: kappa = (agree - expfreq) / (N - expfreq) where agree = sum of utterance-set intersections per category, N = union utterance count. NOT a standard cross-tabulation kappa — it is a Fleiss-style agree/expected calculation per the cited PDF (https://psych.unl.edu/psycrs/handcomp/hckappa.PDF).
kappa.html (rendered output, git d99e9f5) reports: diachronic kappa = 0.82 (strong agreement), synchronic kappa = 0.60 (moderate agreement). Reference: McHugh (2012) thresholds.

Diachronic CSVs structure: columns Speaker, #, Utterance, Moment, IDU, Criteria. The Moment column is the experienced-moment ORDER (integer 1–7 for kev, 1–6 with recode for yesesvi). Utterance→Moment IS the ordering signal for Kendall tau computation. Kev assigned 7 distinct moments; yesesvi assigned 6 (with moment 6 recoded to 7 per kappa.Rmd line: mutate(Moment = recode(Moment, '6' = '7'))).

Ordering recovery status from IRR CSVs: YES — both utterance→IDU assignment (IDU column name strings) and utterance→Moment (experienced order integer) are explicit in kev-diachronic-analysis.csv and yesesvi-diachronic-analysis.csv. Kendall tau between kev and yesesvi moment orderings on p3s1 is COMPUTABLE from git-recovered CSVs.

Kev's diachronic IDU sequence for p3s1 (experienced order by Moment 1→7): IDU1='Putting hands out' (utt 8); IDU2='Imagining a force' (utts 9,11,19,20,21,22.1); IDU3='Felt hands being attracted together' (utt 38); IDU4='Hands moved' (utts 4,15.2,16,17,39,40); IDU5='Surprised by hand movement' (utt 15.1); IDU6='Tried to stay in their head' (utt 22.3); IDU7='Became conscious of experiment' (utts 22.2,23,24,25,26,27,28,31,32,34,35,36). Experimenter utterances filtered: {10,21,23,29,12,14,16,19,39,27,31,33,35,37,25}.

Yesesvi's diachronic IDU sequence for p3s1 (experienced order by Moment 1→6, after recode moment6→7): IDU1='Putting hanfds out'(utt 8); IDU2='Image'(utts 9,10,11,20,21,22,23,29,30); IDU3='Attraction between hands'(utt 38); IDU4='Felt hands move'(utts 4,12,13,14,15,16,17,19,39,40); IDU5='Surprise'(utt 15a); IDU6='Focus shifted'(utts 22a,22b,24,26,27,28,31,32,33,34,35,36). NOTE: yesesvi used 6 moments but moment 6 was recoded to 7 — so effectively same range post-recode.

Human-human IRR scope constraint: The ordering-disagreement band is computable for p3s1 ONLY (the single IRR calibration transcript). The 21 Phase 1 per-transcript XLSX files have ONLY ONE human analyst each (kev), so no inter-rater ordering band exists for those. To extend the human band, additional IRR transcripts would need to be obtained from OSF or generated anew.

XLSX format (per convert_osf_analyses.py which read them before removal): Three sheets per file: 'Diachronic Analysis - Participa' (misspelled), 'Diachronic Structure', 'Synchronic Analysis'. Diachronic sheet row structure: Row 0=header text, Row 1=column names (Speaker, #, Utterance, Moment, IDU name, Criteria), Rows 2+=data where IDU name cell is non-empty on first utterance of each IDU. Diachronic Structure sheet: Row 0='Table 1', Row 1=IDU names in cols 1,3,5..., Row 2=Hinge criteria in cols 2,4,6... — EXPERIENCED ORDER is the IDU sequence in this sheet. Synchronic sheet: Row 0='Table 1', Row 1=column names, Rows 2+=data.

Phase 1 had 21 transcripts: p1s1–p7s3 (7 participants × 3 suggestions). Phase 2 had 18 transcripts: p8s1–p13s3 (6 participants × 3 suggestions). All 39 Phase 2 and Phase 1 transcripts had corresponding per-participant XLSX analyses. Phase 1 also had generic diachronic, generic synchronic, global synchronic aggregation XLSX files.

Transcript format matches plugin expected header exactly: Line 1='Participant N, Suggestion N (Scored N/5)', Line 2=blank, Lines 3+=interleaved 'Kevin Sheldrake: ...' and 'P<N>: ...' turns. Utterances are NOT pre-numbered in the raw files — the plugin's transcript_prep/register_offsets step assigns sequential utterance numbers keyed by physical line order.

The experimenter utterance filter list (hardcoded in irr.py lines 69,123, sourced from kappa.Rmd lines 51,53): {10, 21, 23, 29, 12, 14, 16, 19, 39, 27, 31, 33, 35, 37, 25}. These are utterance NUMBERS specific to p3s1 (the IRR transcript) — they correspond to Kevin Sheldrake turns in that transcript. The filter is transcript-specific, not general.

osf-archive/R/ (deleted, recoverable from git d99e9f5) also contained: global synchronic analysis CSVs for pt1 (Phase 1) and pt2 (Phase 2) in subdirs 'global synchronic analysis pt1/' and 'global synchronic analysis pt2/', with files named by DV ('Engages Imagination High/Low/Moderate Response.csv', 'Felt Effect High/Low/Moderate Response.csv') — 12 CSVs total. Also table1 and table4.Rmd with rendered HTML. These are AGGREGATED cross-participant data, not per-transcript.

runs/phase1-2026-05-17/ analyses are LLM-generated scratch, NOT gold standard. normalize_diachronic.py explicitly generates placeholder data for missing input files. The p1s1-diachronic.md shows only 3 IDUs for p1s1 (CLAUDE.md states p1s1 has 9 IDUs by human gold). Do not use runs/ as benchmarking gold.

test_kappa.py (C:/microphenomenograph/microphenomenograph/1.0.0/scripts/test_kappa.py) expects inter-rater CSVs at microphenomenograph/1.0.0/examples/inter-rater/ (kev-diachronic-analysis.csv, yesesvi-diachronic-analysis.csv, kev-synchronic-analysis.csv, yesesvi-synchronic-analysis.csv). This directory does NOT exist in the working tree — tests are skipped (decorated with @pytest.mark.skipif(not INTER_RATER_DIR.exists())). The CSVs must be restored from git history to run IRR calibration tests.

Phase 2 XLSX analyses (p8s1–p13s3) were designated as acceptance test fixtures (held-out from few-shot pool) per the original design (2026-05-17-microphenomenograph.md: 'Phase 2 analyses are held out as acceptance test fixtures'). These are the most valuable for benchmarking since the primary analyst (kev) has never seen them in the plugin's few-shot context.
constraints: ORDERING GOLD DATA: The Moment column (integer, 1-based experienced-moment order) in kev-diachronic-analysis.csv for p3s1 is the only OSF-sourced human ordering sequence recoverable per-utterance. For the 21 Phase 1 per-transcript XLSX analyses, IDU experienced order is the IDU sequence in the 'Diachronic Structure' sheet (wide-format, left-to-right = experienced order), but ONLY kev's assignments are present — no second rater, so no human-human band for those transcripts.

HUMAN-HUMAN BAND SCOPE: Only p3s1 has two human raters. The human-human disagreement band for ordering (Kendall tau between kev and yesesvi moment sequences) is computable only on p3s1. To claim 'matching the human band' for other transcripts, either (a) run a blind second human rater on those transcripts, or (b) define the band as the p3s1 tau gap applied uniformly.

GOLD DATA RECOVERY REQUIRED: All XLSX and CSV gold files must be restored from git (git show d99e9f5:<path>) before the benchmarking experiment can run. The convert_osf_analyses.py script can convert XLSX to markdown but requires openpyxl. The inter-rater CSVs must be copied to microphenomenograph/1.0.0/examples/inter-rater/ for test_kappa.py to run.

EXPERIMENTER UTTERANCE FILTER: The hardcoded filter list {10,21,23,29,12,14,16,19,39,27,31,33,35,37,25} is SPECIFIC to p3s1's utterance numbering. Applying it blindly to other transcripts is wrong. For benchmarking other transcripts, the experimenter turn filter must be derived dynamically from the Speaker column.

YESESVI RECODE: The yesesvi CSVs require utterance renaming (22→22.1, 22a→22.2, 22b→22.3, 15→15.2, 15a→15.1) and moment recode (6→7) before comparison. These recodes are already implemented in irr.py's load_diachronic_csv() but only activate for files with 'yesesvi' in the filename.

IDU COUNT GROUND TRUTH: CLAUDE.md states p1s1=9, p1s2=7, p1s3=6 IDUs by human gold. The runs/phase1 LLM analyses produced only 2-3 IDUs per transcript — they are unreliable. Actual IDU counts must come from recovered XLSX files.

KENDALL TAU METRIC: Kendall tau is NOT implemented in irr.py. It must be added or implemented in a standalone metrics script before the benchmarking experiment can compute ordering similarity. The alignment problem (matching model IDUs to gold IDUs before tau computation) requires Hungarian algorithm or LLM-align; irr.py has an alignment mechanism keyed alternate→primary that could be reused.

KAPPA FORMULA NOTE: The original authors used a non-standard hand-rolled kappa formula (agree = sum of set-intersection sizes per category; N = union utterance count) NOT sklearn's Cohen kappa. The irr.py implementation may produce slightly different values. Reference output is diachronic=0.82, synchronic=0.60 from kappa.html.

PHASE 2 AS HOLD-OUT: Phase 2 XLSX analyses (p8s1–p13s3, 18 files) are the held-out test set per design. They have never been used as plugin few-shot examples. They are the primary benchmarking target. Phase 1 XLSX analyses were intended as few-shot examples and may have been seen by the LLM during plugin design (contamination risk for benchmarking).

TRANSCRIPT NUMBERING: Raw OSF transcripts have no utterance numbers. The plugin assigns them during transcript_prep. The p3s1 IRR CSVs use utterance numbers that must correspond to the physical line ordering in the raw p3s1.txt. The kev CSV uses integer numbers (1, 4, 8, 9, etc.) — these appear to be non-sequential (not every line numbered), suggesting the human analyst numbered only participant/relevant turns, not every Kevin Sheldrake turn. This must be reconciled before offset-based grounding.

GLOBAL SYNCHRONIC R CSVS: osf-archive/R/global synchronic analysis pt1/ and pt2/ contained 12 CSVs keyed by DV focus ('Engages Imagination', 'Felt Effect') × IV category (High/Low/Moderate). These represent the human-analyst cross-participant aggregation and DV focus selection — critical for hypothesis benchmarking but unrelated to the ordering-focused experiment arm.
open_questions: Which transcript is p3s1 in the context of the 21 Phase 1 transcripts, and does the utterance numbering in the kev/yesesvi CSVs match the line-order numbering the plugin would assign during transcript_prep? (The IRR CSVs show non-sequential utterance numbers — e.g., utts 4, 8, 9, 11, 15, 17 — suggesting human analysts may have numbered only participant utterances or numbered from a pre-processed version of the transcript. This must be verified before grounding utterance_refs.)

Should the XLSX gold data be restored to the working tree from git history for the benchmarking experiment? If yes, the preferred restoration path is: git show d99e9f5:osf-archive/Phase\ 1/analyses/p1s1.xlsx > osf-archive/Phase\ 1/analyses/p1s1.xlsx (for each file), then run convert_osf_analyses.py. Confirm which analysis files (Phase 1 only, Phase 2 only, or all 39) are needed.

Is there a second set of IRR transcripts beyond p3s1 on the OSF repository (https://osf.io) that could be downloaded to extend the human-human ordering band to multiple transcripts? The current git history only shows one transcript pair in Inter-rater Reliability/.

For the 'matching the human band' criterion: should the Kendall tau human-human band on p3s1 be used as the universal threshold, or should the experiment restrict 'beat/match' verdict to p3s1 only (where the ground truth two-rater ordering exists)?
The convert_osf_analyses.py script requires openpyxl. Is this installed in the benchmarking environment, or does a requirements file need to be created?

grounding.summary: Four-part audit of the microphenomenograph 1.0.0 plugin tooling for headless single-transcript diachronic runs, irr.py coverage vs gaps for ordering metrics, Python dependency availability, and OSF XLSX-to-markdown gold parsing.
key_facts: DIACHRONIC STANDALONE PATH (verified): A workflow agent can run the diachronic stage on one transcript by (1) calling mpi_step.py init in an empty temp dir with --allow-active-repo-nested flag (bypasses non-empty-worktree guard); (2) the run dir must have git user.name+email set — mpi_step.py refuses with ERROR git_identity_unset if absent; these can be set via git config --local before calling the skill; (3) transcript_prep must complete first — three substeps hash_raw/normalize/register_offsets, each closed via mpi_step.py close (orchestrator-only, no prompt-artifact required); (4) mpi-analyst subagent then runs three diachronic substeps: criteria_grouping, criteria_revision, idu_naming_ordering, each writing artifacts + calling mpi_step.py close --prompt-artifact (required for LLM substeps); (5) mpi_step.py disables hooks via core.hooksPath .git/hooks-disabled, disables GPG signing, sets core.autocrlf false — so headless git commits work cleanly.

DIACHRONIC BLOCKER 1 — utterance_refs span grounding: every IDU in the JSON output must carry non-empty utterance_refs [{transcript_id, utterance_number, byte_start, byte_end, raw_excerpt}] validated against transcripts/offsets/<id>.json (flat-dict, keyed by string utterance number). Missing or empty utterance_refs rejects the close. The offset registry is produced by transcript_prep.register_offsets. A workflow agent calling the mpi-analyst must either pre-run transcript_prep or supply the offset file independently.

DIACHRONIC BLOCKER 2 — prompt_artifact required for LLM substeps: mpi_step.py close enforces --prompt-artifact for all three diachronic substeps (criteria_grouping, criteria_revision, idu_naming_ordering are in LLM_SUBSTEPS). The prompt artifact is a schema_version 2 JSON file capturing the model call; if the workflow agent does not produce this file before calling close, the close will fail with prompt_artifact_required.

DIACHRONIC BLOCKER 3 — no allow_active_repo_nested by default: mpi_step.py init inside the microphenomenograph repo itself (non-empty worktree) exits with ERROR run_inside_active_repo. Workflow agents must pass --allow-active-repo-nested or point --run at a truly empty directory outside the repo. The flag is available (line 242 of mpi_step.py: allow_nested = getattr(args, 'allow_active_repo_nested', False)).

DIACHRONIC BLOCKER 4 — criteria_revision convergence loop: if criteria_revision closes with decision='more_revision_needed', mpi_step.py automatically sets substep status to 'flagged' and blocks idu_naming_ordering. The orchestrator must re-dispatch criteria_revision (capped at 5 passes per SKILL.md). A headless run must handle this loop or guarantee the LLM converges in one pass.

DIACHRONIC FLOW — mpi-init substeps are NOT required for a standalone single-transcript run: the minimal path is mpi_step.py init (bootstrap only) -> transcript_prep 3 substeps -> diachronic 3 substeps. The init.confirm_study_config close (which writes event_groups to manifest) is not a prerequisite for diachronic closes — SUBSTEP_PREREQUISITES in _mpi_schemas.py only checks diachronic.criteria_revision requires criteria_grouping=done, and idu_naming_ordering requires criteria_revision=done.

IRR.PY CAN ALREADY COMPUTE: Krippendorff nominal alpha (alpha_nominal), Cohen's kappa (cohens_kappa), alpha_U boundary-agreement approximation (alpha_unitizing — NOT the canonical length-weighted formula), Adjusted Rand Index (adjusted_rand_index), bootstrap CIs for all four (naive utterance or block bootstrap), alignment mapping from alternate -> primary category labels (compute_coincidence with alignment list), pre-alignment alpha, sensitivity alpha (high-confidence-only). These cover utterance->IDU agreement and IDU partition agreement. irr.py is PURE STDLIB — no scipy, no numpy.

IRR.PY GAP 1 — Kendall tau ABSENT: irr.py has no Kendall tau computation and no import of scipy. The experiment requires Kendall tau between produced moment-order and gold moment-order. scipy.stats.kendalltau is available and callable (verified: scipy 1.17.1 under default `python`). A standalone metrics script (or an addition to irr.py) must add: (a) tau_b computation via scipy.stats.kendalltau, (b) a bootstrap CI for tau, (c) p-value.

IRR.PY GAP 2 — adjacent-pair inversion rate ABSENT: irr.py has no inversion rate function. Inversion rate = fraction of adjacent IDU pairs (i, i+1 in gold moment order) that appear inverted in the model output. This requires a custom function over the aligned ordered lists.

IRR.PY GAP 3 — IDU-to-gold alignment before order comparison: irr.py's existing alignment mechanism (compute_coincidence) maps alternate category LABELS to primary category LABELS (string-to-string via the alignment list produced by the mpi-cross-analyst LLM). For ordering metrics the alignment must map model IDU objects to gold IDU objects so moment-numbers can be compared. The current alignment mechanism is label-only — it does not produce an ordered sequence of (model_moment, gold_moment) pairs. A metrics script must implement: (a) load model IDU list with moment numbers, (b) load gold IDU list with moment numbers, (c) use the irr.py alignment map to identify which model IDU corresponds to which gold IDU, (d) extract parallel (model_moment_rank, gold_moment_rank) sequences, (e) compute kendalltau on those sequences. Alternatively Hungarian-algorithm matching on utterance-set overlap (no LLM needed if utterance_refs are grounded).

IRR.PY GAP 4 — IDU count delta not computed: irr.py does not compute or record the difference between model IDU count and gold IDU count. The experiment requires IDU count vs human counts (p1s1=9, p1s2=7, p1s3=6). This is a trivial addition (len(model_idus) - gold_count) but must be added to the metrics script.

PYTHON DEPS VERIFIED (under default `python`, i.e. the pip-managed environment): scipy 1.17.1 (scipy.stats.kendalltau confirmed callable), numpy 2.3.5, pandas 3.0.2, openpyxl 3.1.5, statsmodels 0.14.6. All available. Note: python3 (Python 3.10.11) resolves to a different environment where scipy is 1.15.3 and numpy is 2.2.6 (ABI mismatch with pandas 3.0.2 causes ValueError on pandas import). Use `python` not `python3` in harness scripts to get the consistent environment.

SCIPY KENDALL TAU CALL SIGNATURE (verified): from scipy.stats import kendalltau; result = kendalltau(x, y); result.statistic gives tau, result.pvalue gives p-value. Works correctly (tested: kendalltau([1,2,3,4],[1,2,4,3]) -> tau=0.667, p=0.333).

CONVERT_OSF_ANALYSES.PY MAPPING: The script maps one XLSX file (named e.g. p1s1.xlsx) to two markdown files: <stem>-diachronic.md and <stem>-synchronic.md. It uses openpyxl to load sheets. Diachronic sheet (named 'Diachronic Analysis - Participa' or 'Diachonic...'): row 0 = header text, row 1 = column names, rows 2+ = data. Columns: speaker, num (#), utterance, moment, idu_name, criteria. IDUs are identified by non-empty idu_name cells; utterance_numbers are accumulated. The idu_counter assigns sequential idu_number. The 'moment' column from the XLSX is extracted per-IDU (first row of IDU only). Diachronic Structure sheet (separate sheet with 'structure' in name): wide format, row 1=IDU names in cols 1,3,5..., row 2=hinges in cols 2,4,6... Synchronic sheet: row 0='Table 1', row 1=col names, rows 2+=data. Columns: idu_name, num, utterance, criteria, isu, isu_2nd.

CONVERT_OSF_ANALYSES.PY GOLD IDU ORDER: The diachronic markdown output table columns are: IDU #, IDU Name, Utterance Numbers, Criteria. The IDU # is a sequential counter assigned by the script in the order rows appear in the XLSX. The XLSX 'Diachronic Structure' sheet gives the experiential (moment) order of IDUs including hinges between adjacent pairs. The script also parses the 'moment' field from the main Diachronic Analysis sheet — this is the human analyst's assigned moment number. Gold moment-order for tau computation should come from the 'moment' column in parse_diachronic(), not from the sequential idu_counter.

OSF ARCHIVE IN THIS CHECKOUT: osf-archive/Phase 1/transcripts/ contains 21 .txt transcript files (p1s1 through p7s3). IRR CSVs and XLSX analysis files are ABSENT from this checkout. The XLSX files (needed for gold standard and for irr.py's load_diachronic_csv) must be sourced separately. This is a critical gap for running gold comparisons.

MPISTEP.PY INIT REFUSAL BYPASS: The flag --allow-active-repo-nested is accepted by the init argparser (cmd_init checks getattr(args, 'allow_active_repo_nested', False)). This allows initializing a run inside the microphenomenograph repo for testing, producing a nested run. This is acceptable for experiment harness use but produces a 'nested_in_active' run_repo_mode in the manifest.

IRR.PY ALIGNMENT MECHANISM FOR IDU-ORDER COMPARISON: The existing alignment list format is [{primary: 'IDU Name A', alternate: 'IDU Name B', confidence: 0.82, rationale: '...'}]. This maps alternate IDU names to primary IDU names. To use this for ordering comparison: (1) extract model IDUs with their moment numbers from the idu_naming_ordering JSON artifact, (2) extract gold IDUs with their moment numbers from the XLSX/markdown, (3) use the alignment map to pair model IDU names to gold IDU names, (4) for each matched pair, record (model_moment, gold_moment), (5) run kendalltau on the resulting paired sequence. Unmatched IDUs on either side cannot contribute to ordering comparison and should be counted separately as IDU-count-delta.
constraints: mpi_step.py init requires git user.name and user.email set locally or globally — harness scripts must set these before calling init (e.g. via git config --local user.name 'Harness' and user.email 'harness@local' in the temp run dir).

mpi_step.py close requires --prompt-artifact for all three diachronic LLM substeps (criteria_grouping, criteria_revision, idu_naming_ordering). The workflow agent generating the analysis must write a schema_version 2 prompt artifact JSON before calling close.

utterance_refs grounding is mandatory at close time for LLM substeps. The transcript_prep.register_offsets step must precede any diachronic close. The offsets file must be a flat-dict {str_utt_num: {byte_start, byte_end}} — the old array format is rejected.

criteria_revision convergence loop: the agent may need up to 5 passes. The harness must detect status='flagged' on criteria_revision and re-dispatch. A simple experiment harness can avoid this by using a single combined criteria_grouping+revision step and always returning decision='converged'.
irr.py uses pure stdlib (no scipy). Any Kendall tau or inversion-rate computation must be in a separate metrics script or a new function added to irr.py that imports scipy only when needed.

Use `python` (not `python3`) in harness scripts to access the consistent environment with scipy 1.17.1, statsmodels 0.14.6, pandas 3.0.2, openpyxl 3.1.5. The python3 binary on this Windows system resolves to Python 3.10.11 with numpy ABI mismatch causing pandas import to fail.

OSF XLSX analysis files are not present in this checkout — they must be provided separately or pre-converted to markdown before the experiment harness can compare model output to gold. The irr.py load_diachronic_csv function expects the CSV format from osf-archive/Inter-rater Reliability/, which is also absent.

The mpi-analyst agent declares tools: Read, Write, Bash — it is a subagent, not a standalone script. A workflow agent must invoke it as an agent call (via agent() in the workflow script), not as a CLI command. The agent writes its own artifacts and calls mpi_step.py close internally.

Moment numbers in the gold XLSX come from the 'moment' column in the Diachronic Analysis sheet, not from the sequential idu_number counter assigned by parse_diachronic(). The metrics script must use the 'moment' field for ordering comparison, not the IDU row-order index.

For headless yolo-mode runs, mpi_step.py disables pre-commit hooks (core.hooksPath .git/hooks-disabled) and GPG signing (commit.gpgsign false) locally in the run repo. These settings are never applied globally.
open_questions: Are the OSF XLSX analysis files (gold diachronic analyses) and Inter-rater Reliability CSVs available anywhere in the project or must they be downloaded separately? They are absent from the osf-archive/ in this checkout.

What is the intended alignment mechanism for model IDUs vs gold IDUs in the metrics script — LLM-align via a mpi-cross-analyst call (which produces the {primary, alternate, confidence, rationale} format already consumed by irr.py), or utterance-overlap Hungarian matching (no LLM, deterministic)?

Should Kendall tau and inversion rate be added as new functions inside irr.py (breaking its pure-stdlib constraint by importing scipy conditionally), or placed in a new standalone metrics_ordering.py script?

For the 'beating' adjudication mechanism: who or what serves as the blind judge for disagreed orderings? The design references blind judge panels or internal-consistency scoring against temporal cues — has a specific mechanism been chosen?

The criteria_revision convergence loop (up to 5 passes) complicates headless automation. Should the experiment harness suppress this loop by pre-configuring a single-pass mode, or should it handle the full loop?

MINIMAL RUNNER-SCRIPT CONTRACT — run_cell(model_config, scaffold_id, transcript_path, out_dir, seed, timestamp) -> {"artifact_path": str, "cost_log_path": str, "status": "ok"|"skip"|"error"}:

  Idempotency: derive cell_key = sha256(model_id + scaffold_id + transcript_stem); if out_dir/cell_key.json exists, return {"status":"skip","artifact_path":...} immediately.

  Provider dispatch:
    - claude: anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=os.environ[api_key_env]).messages.create(model=model_id, max_tokens=..., messages=[...]) — usage.input_tokens/output_tokens available.
    - gemini (2.5): google.genai client, GenerationConfig(thinking_config=ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=N), temperature=1.0, max_output_tokens=..., response_mime_type="application/json") — Gemini 2.5 uses thinkingBudget(int); DO NOT pass thinkingLevel string or API returns HTTP 400.
    - gemini (3.x): GenerationConfig(thinking_config=ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="low"|"medium"|"high"), temperature=1.0, max_output_tokens=...) — 3.x uses thinkingLevel(string); DO NOT pass thinkingBudget int.
    - deepseek: openai.OpenAI(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.deepseek.com").chat.completions.create(model=model_id, response_format={"type":"json_object"}, messages=[...]) — parse JSON from content, validate against schema client-side; do NOT use .parse() or json_schema response_format.
    - qwen-thinking: two sequential calls — call 1 with enable_thinking=True (or equivalent) to get reasoning; call 2 with json_object response_format to extract structured output from reasoning. If via OpenRouter: use openai SDK with base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1".

  Windows unicode contract: all file writes MUST use open(..., encoding='utf-8'); json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False); transcript reads MUST specify encoding='utf-8'. cp1252 default WILL crash on α, κ, smart-quotes, and non-ASCII transcript content.

  Cost log schema: {"cell_key": str, "model_id": str, "scaffold_id": str, "transcript": str, "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int, "thinking_tokens": int|null, "usd_cost": float|null, "timestamp": str} — usd_cost computes as (input_tokens * price_in + output_tokens * price_out) where price table is supplied externally; flag null if pricing table absent.

  Artifact schema (per cell): {"cell_key": str, "model_id": str, "scaffold_id": str, "transcript": str, "idus": [{"idu_id": str, "utterances": [str], "moment_label": str, "temporal_position": int}], "raw_response": str, "schema_valid": bool, "timestamp": str}

  Metrics (computed post-collection, not in run_cell): Kendall tau requires ADDING to irr.py or a standalone metrics.py (irr.py has no kendall tau function — it has load_diachronic_csv, compute_irr, alpha_nominal, cohens_kappa, alpha_unitizing, adjusted_rand_index, bootstrap_ci, aggregate_stratum_records only). IDU alignment before tau: irr.py has alternate->primary alignment keyed by position; extend or reuse for model->gold alignment. Adjacent-pair inversion rate: compute from ranked IDU list. Schema validity rate: from artifact schema_valid field across cells.

  Known dead cells (do not schedule): Gemini Flash + atomic decomposition + explicit interview-vs-experience prompt + per-segment justification = insufficient (per shared context).

  Concurrency: cap at min(16, cores-2) per workflow constraint; Gemini thinkingBudget cells are slow — budget extra time per cell.

phases.title: Phase 0 — Harness Build and Unit Tests
phases.what: Write and green-test all deterministic Python scripts that every subsequent phase calls. Hard barrier: no agent cells fire until all unit tests pass. Scripts: (1) gold_recovery.py — git-show loop restoring 9 IRR CSVs from d99e9f5 (osf-archive/Inter-rater Reliability/*) and 39 XLSX files (Phase 1/analyses/p1s1.xlsx through Phase 2/analyses/p13s3.xlsx) and 18 Phase 2 transcript .txt files, all via subprocess git show piped to binary write; all paths URL-decoded (no shell escaping needed, use git show with exact path); outputs to scratch/gold/. (2) parse_gold.py — openpyxl-based XLSX parser producing gold JSON: per-transcript list of IDUs with name, utterance-number list, moment-int (from 'moment' column in Diachronic Analysis sheet, first row of each IDU block), validated against Diachronic Structure sheet sequence; outputs scratch/gold/<stem>-diachronic.json. (3) metrics.py — standalone: hungarian_align(model_idus, gold_idus) using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on Jaccard overlap of utterance sets; kendall_tau(model_ranked, gold_ranked) via scipy.stats.kendalltau returning tau_b+pvalue; adjacent_inversion_rate(model_ranked, gold_ranked); idu_count_delta(model, gold); schema_validity(artifact_dict, schema); bootstrap_tau_ci(pairs, n=2000, seed=42) via numpy random.default_rng; reproduce_kappa() loading p3s1 CSVs via irr.py load_diachronic_csv and checking diachronic=0.82+-0.02, synchronic=0.60+-0.02. (4) run_cell.py — idempotent cell runner: cell_key=sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_stem); if scratch/cells/cell_key.json exists return skip; dispatches to Claude (anthropic SDK) or blocked arms (returns status=skip, reason=key_absent); writes artifact JSON and cost log with explicit encoding='utf-8' throughout; seed and timestamp are CLI args not computed at runtime. (5) precompute_shuffles.py — for scaffold S6 (shuffled-input ordering step): seeded RNG (seed=42) generates N-per-transcript permutations; writes scratch/shuffles/<stem>.json; must run before any S6 cells. Unit tests (pytest): test reproduce_kappa (validates full gold recovery+parse chain on p3s1; must hit 0.82+-0.02 and 0.60+-0.02); test hungarian_align on kev-vs-yesesvi p3s1 pairs (Putting hands out <-> Putting hanfds out must match); test kendalltau fixture ([1,2,3,4],[1,2,4,3])->0.667; test idempotency (run_cell twice, second returns skip); test encoding (write alpha+kappa to utf-8 file, read back); test shuffle determinism (same seed same permutation). designs.gold_handling:
HUMAN FALLIBILITY TREATMENT: The OSF primary analyst (kev) is treated as one rater, not ground truth. Gold analyses from XLSX files are kev's assignments -- single-rater, not authoritative.

HUMAN-HUMAN BAND (p3s1 only): kev-diachronic-analysis.csv and yesesvi-diachronic-analysis.csv from osf-archive/Inter-rater Reliability/ (recovered from git d99e9f5) provide two human orderings on transcript p3s1. Band computation: (1) load both CSVs via irr.py load_diachronic_csv with yesesvi recode (utterances 22->22.1/22a->22.2/22b->22.3/15->15.2/15a->15.1; moment 6->7 per kappa.Rmd line 51,53); (2) align IDUs by utterance-set Jaccard (hungarian_align in metrics.py): matches 'Putting hands out' <-> 'Putting hanfds out' etc. to produce 6 matched pairs; (3) extract parallel (kev_moment, yesesvi_moment) sequences; (4) scipy.stats.kendalltau -> tau_hh; (5) bootstrap_tau_ci n=2000 seed=42 to produce (ci_lo, ci_hi); output to scratch/human_band.json. This band (tau_hh, ci_lo, ci_hi) is the only empirical human-human ordering disagreement measure. It is computed from 1 transcript with 6 matched IDU pairs -- bootstrap CI acknowledges n=1 limitation explicitly.

BAND EXTRAPOLATION POLICY: For 18 Phase 2 transcripts (single rater kev only), the p3s1 human band is applied as a stated uniform assumption (model-vs-kev tau compared against the p3s1 ci_lo/ci_hi as a proxy). Reports clearly flag: band_source=p3s1_single_transcript, extrapolation=uniform_assumption. No fraudulent precision claimed.

MODEL-TO-GOLD ALIGNMENT (before tau computation): Model artifacts carry IDUs with utterance_refs (grounded utterance numbers from transcript_prep offsets). Gold JSON carries IDUs with utterance number lists from XLSX parse. Alignment method: (1) build utterance-set for each model IDU from utterance_refs[].utterance_number; (2) build utterance-set for each gold IDU; (3) compute Jaccard similarity matrix (n_model x n_gold); (4) scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on (1 - Jaccard) as cost matrix; (5) pairs with Jaccard < 0.1 flagged as unmatched (excluded from tau, counted in IDU count delta). This is deterministic, no LLM-align needed, because utterance_refs are grounded byte-level to the transcript. The irr.py alternate->primary string-alignment mechanism is NOT reused for this (it is label-only); the Jaccard-Hungarian approach is in standalone metrics.py.

BEAT ADJUDICATION MECHANISM: For cells where model tau exceeds tau_hh_ci_hi on p3s1 (model beats the human-human inter-rater ceiling): (1) extract IDU pairs where model ordering disagrees with kev; (2) present both orderings blind (A=kev, B=model, no labels) to a judge LLM (different model than the one being judged); (3) judge reads only the raw transcript spans from utterance_refs for the disputed IDUs (no analyst labels visible); (4) 3 independent judge calls, majority vote; (5) beat=true if model wins majority of disputed pairs. Methodological caveat logged in every adjudication result: transcript records verbal report, not direct experience; experienced-moment order may be ambiguous or indeterminate from text alone. For 18 Phase 2 transcripts (kev only, single rater), no empirical upper band exists -- beat cannot be claimed with adjudication only; report as beat_candidate with caveat insufficient_irr_coverage_for_phase2.

designs.token_estimate: Rough budget by phase: Phase 0 (harness build): 1 orchestrator agent, ~15k tokens (script writes + pytest iteration). Phase 1 (gold recovery): 1 agent, ~6k tokens. Phase 2 (cell execution): 40 Arm1 mpi-analyst agents x ~8k = 320k; 1 coordinator agent ~5k; Arm2 run_cell.py via Bash (not agents) ~0 agent tokens but ~190 API call costs outside the workflow token budget. Phase 3 (metrics): 1 agent, ~4k tokens (all deterministic Python). Phase 3.5 (adjudication): 0-15 judge agents x ~3k each = 0-45k. Phase 4 (report): 1 agent, ~6k tokens. Total workflow agent tokens: ~400k tokens. Note: Arm2 API calls (run_cell.py) consume Anthropic API tokens at Claude Haiku/Sonnet rates outside the orchestrator budget -- estimate 190 cells x 3k tokens average = 570k tokens API cost tracked in cost logs. Grand total token consumption including API: ~1M tokens, dominated by Arm1 and Arm2 cell execution. Arm3/4/5 blocked so 0 tokens from those arms in initial run.
designs.resumability: Two parallel idempotency mechanisms: (1) API-arm cells (run_cell.py): cell_key = sha256(model_id + scaffold_id + transcript_stem); if scratch/cells/cell_key.json exists on disk, run_cell.py returns {status: skip, artifact_path: existing_path} immediately without calling the API. Workflow coordinator checks this before dispatching. Crash recovery: rerun workflow from phase 2; all completed cells are skipped, only failed/missing cells execute. (2) Arm1 (mpi-analyst skill): mpi_step.py close writes audit events and manifest updates inside a per-run git repo at scratch/runs/<stem>/. Each substep close is a git commit with a unique close_id. If the agent is interrupted mid-substep, rerunning the workflow agent checks manifest substep status; completed substeps (status=done in manifest) are skipped via the existing PREREQ and status-check gates in mpi_step.py. The coordinator must call mpi_step.py verify before re-dispatching to detect partially-complete runs. (3) Timestamps: phase_start_ts is computed once by the workflow JS at the start of each phase and passed as an argument string to all run_cell.py calls in that phase -- no JS Date() calls inside agent loops. (4) S6 shuffles: precomputed to scratch/shuffles/<stem>.json with seed=42 before any S6 cell fires; shuffle files are read-only inputs, never regenerated. (5) Verifier-fallback for Arm1 agents: after each mpi-analyst agent call, orchestrator runs `python mpi_step.py verify --run scratch/runs/<stem>/` and reads manifest to confirm idu_naming_ordering status=done. If agent structured return is empty/malformed but verify confirms done, workflow extracts artifact path from manifest and proceeds (durable side-effects in git take precedence over agent return). (6) Backfill: when blocked-arm keys arrive, rerunning phase 2 automatically fills only the missing cells (existing cell_key.json files are skipped). Phase 3 and 4 re-run cleanly on the augmented scratch/cells/ directory. No state needs to be manually reconciled.
risks: Human-human band n=1: tau_hh and its bootstrap CI come from a single transcript (p3s1, 6 IDU pairs). The CI reflects resampling variance over those 6 pairs, not across transcripts. Any 'match' verdict for non-p3s1 transcripts is an extrapolation under a stated uniform assumption -- not an empirical claim. Report must foreground this limitation.

Experienced-moment order is not directly observable in transcript text: the deep methodological hole for the BEAT adjudication. Transcript records verbal report of experience (interview order), not the structure of the experience itself. A judge LLM reading transcript spans may be reasoning about narrative order, not experienced-moment order. Adjudication verdicts carry irreducible uncertainty; they cannot distinguish a better ordering from a differently-wrong ordering.

criteria_revision non-convergence loop in Arm1: if mpi-analyst's criteria_revision closes with decision=more_revision_needed, the substep is flagged and idu_naming_ordering is blocked. Harness caps at 2 passes and forces decision=converged on pass 2 (via a modified prompt or direct manifest override) to avoid infinite loops. If convergence is forced, record forced_convergence=true in cell metadata and interpret tau results with caution.

JSON truncation in API arms: LLMs generating large JSON IDU lists may truncate mid-object, producing invalid JSON. run_cell.py catches json.JSONDecodeError, records schema_valid=false, and logs raw_response for inspection. Generous max_tokens (8192+) reduces but does not eliminate risk. Track schema_valid% per arm+scaffold as a quality signal.

Phase 1 contamination: XLSX analyses for p1s1-p7s3 were used during plugin design (convert_osf_analyses.py converted them to examples/analyses/ markdown). The LLM may have seen these analyses in its training or in few-shot context. Results for Phase 1 transcripts (Arm2 cells) should be interpreted as upper-bound contamination estimates, not held-out benchmarks. Phase 2 (p8-p13) is the clean test set.

Hand-rolled kappa vs irr.py kappa drift: the original kappa.Rmd uses a non-standard formula (agree = sum of per-category utterance-set intersection sizes; N = union count) not sklearn or standard cross-tabulation. irr.py cohens_kappa may compute a different value. The Phase 0 unit test reproduce_kappa with tolerance 0.82+-0.02 / 0.60+-0.02 validates the entire pipeline, but if irr.py uses a different algorithm, the test may fail requiring a custom kappa function matching kappa.Rmd exactly.

Blocked arms delay full matrix: Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen arms cannot run without user-supplied API keys. The workflow produces partial results immediately (Claude arms only); blocked cells return skip status. The cost-quality frontier and cross-model comparisons are incomplete until keys are provided. This is a design limitation, not a bug -- state clearly in the report.

Utterance numbering mismatch between plugin and gold: raw transcripts have no utterance numbers. Plugin transcript_prep assigns sequential numbers by physical line order. IRR CSVs (kev, yesesvi) used a different numbering (only participant/relevant turns numbered, not every Kevin Sheldrake turn). Jaccard-based alignment in metrics.py handles this gracefully for most IDUs, but IDUs with small utterance sets (1-2 utterances) may have low Jaccard even when correctly matched, producing false unmatched counts. Monitor unmatched_rate per transcript as a diagnostic.

designs.lens: AGENT-NATIVE: each matrix cell is an agent doing work directly (Claude arms via native skill pipeline or direct API calls in Python harness scripts; external arms via Bash/Python calls). Verifier agents check durable side effects after each cell. Small structured returns carry paths+status only; durable detail goes to files.
designs.name: MPI Diachronic Ordering Experiment — Match/Beat the Human Analyst

phases.title: Phase 0 — Harness Bootstrap
phases.what:
Recover all gold data from git history. Establish canonical utterance numbering. Parse gold IDU tables. Compute p3s1 human-human band. Precompute S6 shuffles. Write metrics.py. Build cell manifest.

(a) Git recovery: `git show d99e9f5:<path>` for each of the 39 XLSX analyses (Phase 1: 21 transcripts; Phase 2: 18 transcripts), 4 IRR CSVs (kev-diachronic, kev-synchronic, yesesvi-diachronic, yesesvi-synchronic), and all 18 Phase-2 .txt transcripts (Phase 1 transcripts already present in working tree). Write recovered files to a phase 0 scratch dir `experiment/gold/` and `experiment/transcripts/`.

(b) Canonical numbering: for each transcript, run the plugin's transcript_prep.register_offsets in a disposable temp run dir to get raw-line-order byte-span anchored utterance numbers. Write `experiment/numbering/<id>.json` keyed by string utterance number. For p3s1 specifically, reconcile gold CSV utterance numbers (human-assigned, non-sequential) to canonical line numbers via a matching pass in metrics.py.

(c) Gold parse: for each XLSX, extract IDU table rows using openpyxl. Gold moment order = `moment` column from the Diachronic Analysis sheet (NOT the sequential idu_counter). Write `experiment/gold/<id>-diachronic.json` with schema {transcript_id, idus: [{idu_id, name, moment_int, utterance_numbers_gold, utterance_numbers_canonical}]}.

(d) p3s1 human-human band: load kev and yesesvi diachronic CSVs; apply yesesvi recodes (22→22.1, 22a→22.2, 22b→22.3, 15→15.2, 15a→15.1; moment 6→7); align IDUs by Hungarian on utterance-set Jaccard; compute Kendall tau (scipy.stats.kendalltau) on aligned (kev_moment, yesesvi_moment) pairs; compute adjacent-pair inversion rate; bootstrap 2000 reps (seeded=42) for 95% CI. Write `experiment/gold/p3s1-human-band.json`.

(e) Write `experiment/metrics.py`: kendall_tau(model_moments, gold_moments), adjacent_pair_inversion_rate(aligned_pairs), idu_count_delta(model_n, gold_n), hungarian_align(model_idus, gold_idus) via utterance-set Jaccard, grounding_integrity(idus), cost_per_transcript(cost_log).

(f) S6 shuffles: precompute seeded RNG (seed=42) shuffled utterance orderings for each transcript in the benchmark subset; write to `experiment/shuffles/<id>-s6-ordering.json`. Timestamps for all cells: generate ISO8601 string once in harness, pass via cell manifest.

(g) Cell manifest: build `experiment/cells.json` listing all cells with status: Claude arms (Arm1 native, Arm2 Haiku/Sonnet) × scaffolds S1-S6 × benchmark transcripts × reps 1-3. Non-Claude arms (Arm3 Gemini, Arm4 DeepSeek, Arm5 Qwen) listed with status=skip, reason=api_key_missing. Known dead cell listed with status=skip, reason=known_dead. Idempotency key = sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_id+rep_number).

Benchmark subset: p3s1 (human-band anchor, Phase 1, Moderate-IV); p8s1 (Phase 2 Low-IV held-out); p10s1 (Phase 2 Moderate-IV held-out); p12s1 (Phase 2 High-IV held-out); p1s1 (Phase 1, contamination-flagged sanity check, known 9 IDUs); p1s2 (Phase 1, contamination-flagged sanity check, known 7 IDUs); p1s3 (Phase 1, contamination-flagged sanity check, known 6 IDUs). 7 transcripts total in headline subset.
phases.agents: 2 sequential agents, no concurrency needed. Agent-A (git-recovery, model=claude-sonnet-4-6, label=phase0-recovery): runs all git show commands, writes recovered files, no structured return beyond {status, files_written: [...]}. Agent-B (harness-writer, model=claude-sonnet-4-6, label=phase0-harness): writes experiment/metrics.py, experiment/run_cell.py, experiment/align.py (Hungarian implementation), computes p3s1 human band, precomputes shuffles, builds cells.json; returns {status, human_band: {tau_point, tau_ci_lower, tau_ci_upper, inversion_rate, n_aligned_pairs}}. Both agents have all tools including Bash (use `python` not `python3`). Phase 0 is purely sequential and single-threaded — the cell manifest is the output product. Estimated 10k-20k tokens per agent call.

phases.title: Phase 1 — Cell Execution (Claude Arms Only)
phases.what:
Execute all runnable Claude-arm cells from cells.json. Each cell is idempotent: check if `experiment/cells/<cell_key>.json` already exists; if so return {status:skip, artifact_path:...} immediately. Two cell types:

Arm 1 (native mpi-analyst pipeline): For each (transcript × scaffold × rep) cell where scaffold=S1 and arm=native: (1) git init a temp run dir under `experiment/runs/<cell_key>/`; (2) set local git config user.name+user.email; (3) call mpi_step.py init --allow-active-repo-nested; (4) run transcript_prep (3 substeps: hash_raw, normalize, register_offsets — orchestrator-only, no prompt artifact); (5) run diachronic via mpi-analyst subagent (3 substeps: criteria_grouping, criteria_revision, idu_naming_ordering; subagent writes its own artifacts + calls mpi_step.py close --prompt-artifact); handle criteria_revision loop (status=flagged → re-dispatch, cap 5 passes); (6) verify durable side effects by reading manifest + audit.jsonl (verifier-fallback: if agent return is empty/malformed, read the run dir directly); (7) write `experiment/cells/<cell_key>.json` with {cell_key, arm, scaffold, transcript, model_id, idu_list_path, run_dir, status, timestamp}. Each Arm1 cell is a 2-agent pipeline (mpi-analyst sub, verifier). The verifier is a lightweight reader-only agent that reads manifest+artifacts and emits {idu_count, idus_with_utterance_refs, artifact_paths}.

Arm 2 (direct API tiers via run_cell.py): For each (transcript × scaffold × rep) cell where arm=claude-haiku-4-5 or claude-sonnet-4-6: agent calls `python experiment/run_cell.py --cell-key <key> --model <id> --scaffold <id> --transcript <path> --gold <path> --shuffle <path|null> --timestamp <iso> --seed <int>`. run_cell.py: loads transcript, applies scaffold prompt, calls anthropic API directly, validates response JSON against artifact schema, writes artifact and cost log, returns {status, artifact_path, cost_log_path}. Scaffolds S1-S6 are prompt templates; S6 injects precomputed shuffle order.

S2 (global timeline-first): prompt preamble asks for experienced-moment timeline reconstruction before IDU assignment.
S3 (forced permutation+justification): prompt asks model to enumerate all possible orderings of a candidate set and justify selection.
S4 (adjacent-pair self-verification): after IDU ordering, model re-reads adjacent pairs and verifies each transition is a genuine moment boundary.
S6 (shuffled input): utterances presented in precomputed shuffled order; model must assign IDUs then order by experienced moment.

Concurrency: max(1, min(16, cpu_count-2)) cells in parallel per workflow. Arm1 cells (full pipeline) run sequentially per transcript to avoid git-lock collisions in the run dir — they parallelize across different transcripts. Arm2 cells parallelize freely.
phases.agents: Per Arm1 cell: 1 mpi-analyst subagent (model: native, has Write+Bash+Read tools; runs full pipeline internally) + 1 verifier reader-agent (model=claude-haiku-4-5, reads run dir only, lightweight). Per Arm2 cell: 1 harness-runner agent (model=claude-sonnet-4-6, has Bash, calls `python experiment/run_cell.py ...`). Arm2 runner agents parallelize up to concurrency cap. Total estimated agents Phase 1: 7 transcripts × (1 scaffold for Arm1 native S1 + 5 scaffolds for Arm2) × 2 models (Haiku/Sonnet for Arm2) × 3 reps = 7×1×1×3 = 21 Arm1 cells + 7×5×2×3 = 210 Arm2 cells = ~231 agent pairs. In practice most Arm1 scaffolds S2-S6 are not applicable to native pipeline (S1 only for Arm1). Haiku budget per Arm2 call ~3k tokens; Sonnet ~6k tokens.

phases.title: Phase 2 — Per-Cell Metrics (Verify as Cells Complete)
phases.what:
For each completed cell artifact, compute: (a) Hungarian alignment of model IDUs to gold IDUs (utterance-set Jaccard, deterministic); (b) Kendall tau on aligned (model_moment, gold_moment) pairs via scipy.stats.kendalltau; (c) adjacent-pair inversion rate; (d) IDU count delta (model_n - gold_n); (e) utterance-level Krippendorff alpha (reuse irr.py.alpha_nominal on the aligned partition); (f) grounding integrity (% IDUs with non-empty utterance_refs where byte ranges verify against raw transcript); (g) schema validity (schema_valid flag from cell artifact). Each metric agent reads one cell artifact + the corresponding gold JSON + transcript; writes `experiment/metrics/<cell_key>-metrics.json`; returns {cell_key, status, tau_point, tau_ci_lower, tau_ci_upper, idu_count_delta, alpha_nominal, grounding_pct, schema_valid}. For p3s1 cells only: also compute vs-human-band fields {within_human_band, band_tau_lower, band_tau_upper}. Non-p3s1 transcripts: compute distance-to-gold (tau) only; NO band claim (explicitly flagged in output as single-rater-gold, no band). Experimenter-turn filter: derived dynamically from the Speaker column of the gold CSV (not the hardcoded p3s1-specific filter list) for all other transcripts.

Verification pipeline: a sweep agent runs after each transcript's cells complete, reading all metrics files for that transcript, checking for anomalies (e.g. tau=1.0 on all reps of one arm = likely idempotency bug not genuine rep), flagging and writing `experiment/metrics/<transcript_id>-sweep.json`.
phases.agents: One metrics-compute agent per cell (model=claude-haiku-4-5, Bash only, runs `python experiment/metrics.py --cell-key <key> ...`). One sweep agent per transcript (model=claude-haiku-4-5). Parallelize metrics agents up to concurrency cap. Estimated ~231 metrics agents + 7 sweep agents. Each metrics agent: ~1k tokens (just a Bash call and a JSON read). Sweep agent: ~2k tokens.

phases.title: Phase 3 — Adjudication + Band Calibration
phases.what:
For each p3s1 cell where the model's ordering disagrees with kev's gold AND the disagreement is outside the human-human band: run a blind judge agent. The judge receives: (a) the raw transcript; (b) two anonymized orderings (human=kev vs model, labeled 'Analyst A' and 'Analyst B' via seeded random assignment per cell to prevent systematic bias); (c) explicit instruction to pick which ordering better reflects experienced-moment order based solely on temporal cues in the transcript (lexical markers: 'then', 'after', 'suddenly', 'before that', etc.); (d) option to declare a tie (tie → within-band verdict). Judge outputs: {preferred: 'A'|'B'|'tie', reasoning: str, temporal_cues_cited: [str]}. Beat = model wins more adjudicated disagreements than it loses; Tie = within-band. Judge model: claude-sonnet-4-6 (stronger than haiku for nuanced temporal reasoning). Each judge agent handles exactly one (model_ordering vs kev_ordering) pair.

For non-p3s1 transcripts: no adjudication (single-rater gold only). The report explicitly states: 'No human-human band exists for this transcript. Distance-to-gold (Kendall tau vs kev) reported as a single-rater similarity score, not a match/beat verdict.' This policy is option (c) from the possible approaches: restrict the headline match/beat claim to p3s1; treat Phase-2 transcripts as single-rater distance-to-gold only. Rationale: option (a) (apply p3s1 tau gap uniformly) is an untested assumption; option (b) (adjudication panel for all non-p3s1 transcripts) is cost-prohibitive; the single-rater distance is still informative as a consistency signal.

Band calibration: after all p3s1 cells complete, compute the empirical distribution of model tau values across arms × scaffolds × reps. Overlay the human band (from Phase 0). Compute: fraction of cells within band per arm; fraction above band (potential beat candidates, adjudicated in this phase); fraction below band. Write `experiment/band-calibration.json`.
phases.agents: One judge agent per disagreed p3s1 cell pair (model=claude-sonnet-4-6, Read+Bash tools, reads transcript and the two anonymized orderings). Estimated upper bound: 1 arm × 6 scaffolds × 2 models × 3 reps × 1 disagreed transcript = ~36 judge pairs (minus ties and within-band cells). One band-calibration aggregator agent (model=claude-haiku-4-5, Bash only, runs Python aggregation script). Agents parallelize freely. ~36×4k tokens = ~144k tokens for judge agents.

phases.title: Phase 4 — Synthesis and Report
phases.what: One synthesis agent reads all per-cell metrics, band calibration JSON, and judge verdicts to produce: (a) `experiment/report/match-beat-verdict.json` — per-arm/scaffold match rate (p3s1 only), beat rate (p3s1 adjudicated), distance-to-gold summary (all transcripts); (b) `experiment/report/cost-quality-frontier.json` — tau × cost per transcript per arm; (c) `experiment/report/idu-count-summary.json` — model IDU count vs gold per arm, including contamination-flagged Phase-1 sanity check rows separately labeled; (d) `experiment/report/final-report.md` — human-readable synthesis with: match/beat verdict section (p3s1 only, with band visualization), distance-to-gold table (all transcripts), cost-quality table, key findings per scaffold, honest limitations section (single-rater gold for non-p3s1, intra-model consistency caveat per irr-fidelity design, Phase-1 contamination flag, utterance-numbering reconciliation assumptions). Returns {status, report_paths: [...]}.
phases.agents: One synthesis agent (model=claude-sonnet-4-6, Read+Bash+Write tools). Reads experiment/metrics/*.json, experiment/band-calibration.json, experiment/gold/p3s1-human-band.json, experiment/report/* (writes). Estimated ~8k tokens (heavy reading, structured JSON in, markdown out). No parallelism needed.

designs.gold_handling:
HUMAN-HUMAN BAND (p3s1 only):
Kendall tau between kev and yesesvi moment orderings is computed on p3s1 exclusively (the only transcript with two human raters in the OSF IRR archive). Procedure: (1) recover kev-diachronic-analysis.csv and yesesvi-diachronic-analysis.csv from git d99e9f5; (2) apply yesesvi recodes in irr.py load_diachronic_csv (22→22.1, 22a→22.2, 22b→22.3, 15→15.2, 15a→15.1; moment 6→7); (3) align IDUs by Hungarian algorithm on utterance-set Jaccard overlap (deterministic, no LLM needed — preferred over irr.py string-label alignment to remove a variance source); (4) extract aligned (kev_moment, yesesvi_moment) pairs; (5) compute Kendall tau via scipy.stats.kendalltau; (6) bootstrap 2000 reps seeded=42 for 95% CI; (7) write experiment/gold/p3s1-human-band.json with {tau_point, tau_ci_lower, tau_ci_upper, inversion_rate_kev_yesesvi, n_aligned_pairs, n_unmatched_kev, n_unmatched_yesesvi}.

MATCH DEFINITION (p3s1): model tau within [tau_ci_lower, tau_ci_upper] of the human-human band = match. Tau above tau_ci_upper = potential beat candidate → adjudicated in Phase 3.

ADJUDICATION FOR BEAT CLAIM (p3s1): Blind judge agent (claude-sonnet-4-6) given raw transcript + two anonymized orderings (kev vs model, labeled A/B via seeded random flip to prevent systematic bias). Judge picks ordering that better reflects experienced-moment order by temporal cues (lexical markers, phenomenological sequence). Tie → within-band. Beat = model wins majority of adjudicated disagreed pairs across reps.

NON-p3s1 TRANSCRIPTS — POLICY CHOICE (c): Restrict headline match/beat claim to p3s1. All other transcripts (Phase-2 held-out p8s1/p10s1/p12s1; Phase-1 contamination-flagged p1s1/p1s2/p1s3) report distance-to-gold as Kendall tau (model vs kev) only — no band claim. Report explicitly labels these as 'single-rater gold; no human-human band available'. Rationale: applying the p3s1 tau gap uniformly (option a) is an untested assumption; adjudicating all 6 non-p3s1 transcripts (option b) is cost-prohibitive and introduces adjudicator variance; option (c) is the most scientifically honest. The distance-to-gold signal is still informative as a consistency metric.

GOLD IDU ORDER SOURCE: `moment` column from the Diachronic Analysis XLSX sheet (NOT the sequential idu_counter assigned by convert_osf_analyses.py). This is the human analyst's experienced-moment assignment (integer, 1-based). The IDU sequence in the 'Diachronic Structure' sheet (wide-format left-to-right) is used as a cross-check.

UTTERANCE NUMBERING RECONCILIATION: Gold XLSX uses human-assigned non-sequential utterance numbers; plugin transcript_prep assigns canonical raw-line-order numbers; API arms number independently. A reconciliation pass in Phase 0 maps gold utterance numbers to canonical numbers via exact-text matching of utterance content (byte-span anchored). This is the largest hidden-effort item — the mapping may be incomplete for utterances that span edits or have whitespace differences. The alignment quality (coverage %) is recorded in the gold parse output and propagated to the per-cell metrics as a data quality flag.

EXPERIMENTER FILTER: The hardcoded set {10,21,23,29,12,14,16,19,39,27,31,33,35,37,25} is p3s1-specific. For all other transcripts, experimenter turns are filtered dynamically by detecting Speaker column = 'Kevin Sheldrake' (or equivalent experimenter label) in the gold CSV. For API arms, experimenter filtering is applied at prompt construction time by stripping Kevin Sheldrake turns from the transcript before injection.

CONTAMINATION FLAG: Phase-1 transcripts (p1s1-p7s3) were intended as plugin few-shot examples and may appear in the LLM training data. Results for p1s1/p1s2/p1s3 are clearly labeled 'contamination-flagged; treat as sanity check only, not held-out benchmark'. Phase-2 transcripts (p8s1-p13s3) are the primary benchmark; they were held-out per the original design.

designs.token_estimate: Phase 0: 2 agents × ~15k tokens = 30k. Phase 1 Arm1: 21 cells × 2 agents (mpi-analyst + verifier) × ~12k tokens avg = 504k. Phase 1 Arm2: 210 cells × 1 runner agent × ~2k tokens = 420k. Phase 2 metrics: 231 agents × ~1k tokens = 231k. Phase 2 sweep: 7 agents × ~2k tokens = 14k. Phase 3 judge: ~36 agents × ~4k tokens = 144k. Phase 3 calibration: 1 agent × 2k = 2k. Phase 4 synthesis: 1 agent × 8k = 8k. Total estimate: ~1.35M tokens. Dominant costs: Phase 1 Arm1 (Sonnet full pipeline × 21 cells) + Phase 1 Arm2 Sonnet cells. At current Sonnet pricing (~$3/Mtok input + $15/Mtok output), budget ~$10-20 for Phase 1 Claude arm cells excluding thinking tokens. Haiku arm is substantially cheaper (~10x). Non-Claude arms blocked, so budget is bounded.
designs.resumability: The workflow journal (cells.json) is the resume checkpoint. Each cell is idempotent: sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_id+rep_number) as key; experiment/cells/<key>.json written atomically (write to .tmp then rename) on completion. On crash: re-run workflow; build_cell_manifest.py re-reads existing artifacts and sets status=done/skip appropriately; in-progress cells restart cleanly (temp run dirs are disposable; Arm1 run dirs under experiment/runs/<cell_key>/ are wiped and re-initialized on restart if manifest status != done). Arm1 native pipeline cells are additionally protected by the mpi_step.py transactional close protocol (artifact + audit + manifest + git commit); the verifier-fallback agent reads the durable run dir rather than trusting agent return values. Phase 0 recovery is idempotent (recover_gold.py skips already-recovered files). Phase 2 metrics are idempotent (metrics agent skips if <cell_key>-metrics.json exists). Phase 3 judges write to experiment/judge/<cell_key>-judge.json before returning; on resume, judge dispatch is skipped for already-judged pairs. Phase 4 synthesis is a single read-then-write with no external state; safe to re-run. Non-deterministic JS time/random is never called in the workflow script — timestamps are generated once by build_cell_manifest.py (Python, seeded), shuffles are precomputed in Phase 0 and read from file by all subsequent phases.
risks: UTTERANCE NUMBERING RECONCILIATION FAILURE: Gold XLSX human-assigned utterance numbers may not match plugin canonical line numbers due to editing differences, whitespace normalization, or non-sequential human numbering. If reconcile_utterances.py coverage < 80% for a transcript, that transcript's Hungarian alignment will be unreliable and tau metrics will be meaningless. Mitigation: report coverage_pct per transcript; exclude cells where coverage < 80% from the match/beat claim; fall back to IDU-name-string matching as secondary alignment for unreconciled IDUs.

PHASE-2 TRANSCRIPT RECOVERY FROM GIT: The 18 Phase-2 .txt transcripts must be recovered via git show d99e9f5. If the path names in git history differ from the assumed osf-archive/Phase 2/transcripts/<stem>.txt pattern, recovery will fail silently. Mitigation: Phase 0 recovery agent enumerates all paths in the d99e9f5 tree first (git ls-tree -r d99e9f5) before constructing show commands.

CRITERIA_REVISION CONVERGENCE LOOP IN ARM1: mpi-analyst may flag criteria_revision as needing-more-revision up to 5 times, dramatically increasing per-cell token cost and wall time. Mitigation: the harness detects status=flagged and re-dispatches up to 5 times per SKILL.md cap; if still flagged after 5 passes, mark cell as status=degraded (not error) and proceed with best available artifact.

IDEMPOTENCY COLLAPSE IN ARM2 REPS: If temperature is not varied across reps, all 3 reps of an Arm2 cell may produce identical outputs, making the rep-variance signal meaningless. Mitigation: rep 1→temp=0.7, rep 2→temp=0.9, rep 3→temp=1.0 passed as explicit CLI args to run_cell.py.

HUMAN-BAND NARROWNESS: If the p3s1 kev/yesesvi ordering disagreement is small (high tau between them), the band will be narrow and most model outputs will fall outside it — making 'match' very hard to achieve. This is an empirical finding not a design flaw, but must be documented honestly in the report.

ADJUDICATOR BIAS IN PHASE 3: Using claude-sonnet-4-6 as the blind judge and also as Arm2b creates a potential self-preference bias (the model may prefer its own style of output). Mitigation: seeded random A/B label assignment per cell; record judge model in verdict JSON; in the report flag that same-model adjudication is an acknowledged limitation.

GOLD XLSX SHEET NAME VARIATION: convert_osf_analyses.py already handles 'Diachonic...' misspelling but there may be additional sheet name variants across 39 XLSX files. Mitigation: parse_gold.py tries exact match first, then substring match for 'diachronic' and 'structure', then emits a warning and skips the file.

PHASE-1 CONTAMINATION AMBIGUITY: p1s1-p7s3 transcripts may have appeared in LLM training data since the OSF project is public. The contamination flag in the report is advisory — there is no definitive way to test for memorization without training data disclosure from Anthropic/providers. Report labels these cells clearly and excludes them from the headline match/beat verdict.

SCIPY IMPORT ON WRONG PYTHON: Using `python3` instead of `python` in any harness script will invoke Python 3.10.11 where pandas 3.0.2 fails to import due to numpy ABI mismatch. All harness scripts must invoke `python` explicitly. Mitigation: experiment/run_cell.py and all experiment/*.py scripts include a shebang `#!/usr/bin/env python` and are invoked via `python script.py` not `python3 script.py`.

phases.title: Phase 0 — Harness bootstrap (scripts + gold recovery)
phases.what: Write all Python harness scripts. Recover OSF gold data from git history (git show d99e9f5:<path>) for all 39 transcripts. Recover and place IRR CSVs for p3s1. Convert Phase-2 XLSX analyses (p8s1-p13s3) to canonical JSON gold via parse_gold.py. Precompute all S6 shuffles with seeded RNG (write shuffle_seeds.json). Precompute all idempotency keys (sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_stem)) and write experiment_cells.json enumerating every cell with skip=true for arms 3-5 (api_key_absent). Run compute_band.py on recovered p3s1 IRR CSVs to produce human_band.json (kev vs yesesvi Kendall tau + annotation). Write power_analysis.py stub that the workflow will call at run-start to compute power given N and k before any cells execute.
phases.agents: 1 agent (claude-sonnet, pipeline=sequential, label=harness-bootstrap). Writes files only, no LLM analysis. Schema return: {status, scripts_written: [str], gold_transcripts_recovered: int, cells_enumerated: int, band_tau: float}. Small return; all detail in files. Budget: ~8k output tokens.

phases.title: Phase 1 — Arm 1 cell execution (current skill implementation)
phases.what: For each Phase-2 transcript (primary target, N=18) and each replication k=3 (seeds precomputed): init a temp run dir with --allow-active-repo-nested, set git identity locally, run transcript_prep 3 substeps (hash_raw, normalize, register_offsets) via mpi_step.py, then dispatch mpi-analyst subagent for diachronic 3 substeps (criteria_grouping, criteria_revision with convergence-loop handling up to 5 passes, idu_naming_ordering). Each substep writes artifacts and calls mpi_step.py close. Idempotency: check cell_key artifact exists before dispatching. Write raw IDU JSON to results/arm1/<transcript>/<seed>/idu_output.json. Also run p3s1 (band-anchor transcript) for arm1 with k=3 replications.
phases.agents: Up to 19 parallel agents (18 Phase-2 + p3s1), each k=3 replications sequential within the agent to honour the convergence loop. Each agent is mpi-analyst shape (Read+Write+Bash tools), claude-sonnet model. Pipeline: barrier after all cells before Phase 2. Schema return per agent: {transcript, seed, status, idu_count, artifact_path}. Token budget: ~40k tokens per transcript-replication (3 substeps x 3 diachronic LLM calls each, generous context). Total arm1: ~19 transcripts x 3 reps x 40k = ~2.3M tokens.

phases.title: Phase 2 — Arm 2 cell execution (Claude API tiers direct)
phases.what: For each Phase-2 transcript x {claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6} x {S1,S2,S3,S4,S6} scaffolds x k=3 replications: call run_cell.py via Bash (not agent()). run_cell.py handles idempotency (skip if cell_key.json exists), provider dispatch (anthropic SDK), utf-8 I/O, structured IDU output with schema validation, cost logging. S6 uses precomputed shuffle_seeds.json. Results land in results/arm2/<model>/<scaffold>/<transcript>/<seed>/. Also run p3s1 for all arm2 cells. Skip known dead cell (atomic-decomp + interview-vs-experience + per-segment justification on any arm -- mark skip_reason in experiment_cells.json). Barriers: wait for Phase 1 before starting; aggregate both arms together in Phase 3.
phases.agents: 1 orchestrating agent per scaffold (5 agents in parallel, each dispatching its transcript batch sequentially via Bash run_cell.py calls). Model: claude-sonnet (orchestrator only; actual LLM calls made by run_cell.py via anthropic SDK). Schema return per orchestrator: {scaffold, cells_run: int, cells_skipped: int, errors: [str]}. Token budget for orchestrators: ~5k each. run_cell.py calls: 18 transcripts x 2 models x 5 scaffolds x 3 reps = 540 cells, each ~8k-20k tokens via API = ~5-11M tokens API-side.

phases.title: Phase 3 — Gold alignment + ordering metrics
phases.what: For every completed cell artifact (arms 1+2): (1) load gold IDU list with moment numbers from recovered XLSX JSON (Phase-2 held-out); (2) align model IDUs to gold IDUs via Hungarian algorithm on utterance-set Jaccard overlap (deterministic, no LLM, no irr.py alignment which has a known inversion bug); (3) extract paired (model_moment_rank, gold_moment_rank) sequences for matched IDUs; (4) compute Kendall tau-b via scipy.stats.kendalltau; (5) compute adjacent-pair inversion rate; (6) compute IDU count delta (model count - gold count); (7) compute utterance-to-IDU agreement (Krippendorff alpha via irr.py alpha_nominal on aligned labels); (8) compute schema-validity rate and grounding-integrity rate. Write per-cell metrics JSONL to results/metrics/<cell_key>.json. Collect all into results/metrics_all.jsonl.
phases.agents: 1 agent (claude-sonnet, Bash-heavy, runs metrics.py via python interpreter). Purely computational, no LLM judgment. Schema return: {cells_processed: int, cells_skipped_no_gold: int, metrics_path: str}. Token budget: ~10k.

phases.title: Phase 4 — Band calibration + power analysis execution
phases.what: Using human_band.json (kev vs yesesvi tau on p3s1, n=1, applied uniformly as stated assumption): compute MATCH criterion (model tau within [kev_tau - band_width/2, kev_tau + band_width/2] per cell). Compute binomial confidence intervals for win-rate > 0.5 per (arm, scaffold) family using BH FDR correction across all cells. Run the power_analysis.py that Phase 0 wrote, passing N=18 (Phase-2 transcripts) and k=3 replications. Record the pre-registered BEAT criterion threshold: lower bound of 95% BCI > 0.5 after BH correction. Write results/inference/band_calibration.json and results/inference/power_report.json.
phases.agents: 1 agent (claude-sonnet, Bash). Schema return: {band_tau_human_human: float, band_width: float, band_n_raters: int, beat_criterion: str, power_at_delta_0_15: float, metrics_path: str}. Token budget: ~5k.

phases.title: Phase 5 — Blind adjudication panel (primary BEAT verdict)
phases.what: For each (arm, scaffold) cell where model tau >= kev gold tau (candidate BEAT cases), and for a stratified sample of 6 Phase-2 transcripts (2 per IV category: low/moderate/high): construct adjudication trials. Each trial: transcript text + two anonymized IDU orderings (model vs gold), order-balanced (A/B randomly from precomputed shuffle_seeds.json). Panel: 3 judge agents, each a DIFFERENT model from the arm being judged (arm1 judged by claude-haiku; arm2 claude-sonnet cells judged by a gemini-class judge if key available, else claude-haiku with caveat recorded). Judges instructed to pick which ordering better fits temporal cues in the transcript; no reference to analyst identity. Aggregate majority vote per trial. Win-rate > 0.5 with BCI lower bound > 0.5 after BH correction = BEAT. Record all judgments to results/adjudication/trials.jsonl.
phases.agents: Up to 3 judge agents per trial (parallel within trial), barrier before aggregating. Trials: up to ~30 candidate BEAT cases x 3 judges = up to 90 agent calls. Model: claude-haiku-4-5 for judges (cheap; arm2 haiku cells judged by a distinct judge model -- use sonnet). Pipeline: fan-out per trial, barrier, aggregate. Schema return per trial: {trial_id, transcript, arm, scaffold, winner, votes: [A|B|tie], judge_models: [str]}. Token budget: ~3k per judge call = ~270k total.

phases.title: Phase 6 — Final report assembly
phases.what: Aggregate all per-cell metrics, band calibration, power report, and adjudication results. Produce: (a) results/report/per_cell_results.jsonl (all cells, all metrics); (b) results/report/match_beat_verdict.json (per arm+scaffold: match_rate, beat_rate, BCI, BH-corrected p-value, verdict); (c) results/report/cost_frontier.json (cost per transcript vs tau per arm); (d) results/report/summary.md (human-readable narrative including the explicit caveat: band estimated from n=1 transcript p3s1, applied uniformly as stated assumption; same-model judging inflates BEAT via correlated errors -- judge model recorded; Phase-1 transcripts contamination-flagged). All arms 3-5 skipped cells are reported as pending with skip_reason=api_key_absent.
phases.agents: 1 agent (claude-sonnet). Schema return: {verdict_path: str, summary_path: str, arms_completed: int, arms_pending: int, cells_total: int, cells_run: int, cells_skipped: int}. Token budget: ~15k.

designs.gold_handling:
GOLD DATA SOURCE: Phase-2 XLSX analyses (p8s1-p13s3) recovered from git history via `git show d99e9f5:osf-archive/Phase 2/analyses/<stem>.xlsx` and parsed by parse_gold.py using openpyxl. Gold moment-order for tau is taken from the `moment` column in the Diachronic Analysis sheet (the human analyst's integer moment-assignment), NOT from the sequential IDU row-order index. Gold IDU list = IDU sequence from Diachronic Structure sheet (wide format, left-to-right = experienced order). Single human analyst per transcript (kev). No second rater on Phase-2 transcripts.

HUMAN-HUMAN BAND (n=1 EXPLICIT CAVEAT): The only transcript with two human raters is p3s1. kev vs yesesvi Kendall tau-b is computed from recovered IRR CSVs (git show d99e9f5:osf-archive/Inter-rater Reliability/kev-diachronic-analysis.csv and yesesvi-diachronic-analysis.csv) with yesesvi recodes applied (utterance renaming 22->22.1, 22a->22.2, 22b->22.3, 15->15.2, 15a->15.1; moment 6->7). Experimenter turns filtered DYNAMICALLY by Speaker column (NOT by the hardcoded {10,21,...} list which is p3s1-specific). The resulting tau gap (|tau_kev - tau_yesesvi| or equivalently the kev-vs-yesesvi tau itself) defines the human-human band. THIS BAND IS ESTIMATED FROM N=1 TRANSCRIPT AND APPLIED UNIFORMLY AS A STATED ASSUMPTION. The report must include this caveat verbatim. MATCH definition: model tau within [tau_human_gold - band_width/2, tau_human_gold + band_width/2] where band_width = 1 - tau_kev_yesesvi (the disagreement gap).

ALIGNMENT BEFORE TAU: Model IDUs are matched to gold IDUs using Hungarian algorithm on utterance-set Jaccard overlap (deterministic, pure Python, no LLM). This is mandatory because: (a) irr.py's LLM-alignment mechanism has a known inversion bug (primary->alternate map used as alternate->primary lookup, unfixed as of this branch); (b) LLM alignment injects nondeterminism into the headline metric. The Hungarian alignment produces a bijection (model_idu_i -> gold_idu_j); unmatched IDUs on either side are counted as IDU-count-delta but excluded from the tau sequence. Tau is computed only over matched pairs.

BEAT VERDICT: Primary mechanism is the blind adjudication panel (Phase 5), not the band comparison. Panel judges see transcript + two anonymized orderings (model vs gold, order-balanced via precomputed shuffles), pick which better fits temporal evidence. Judges are a DIFFERENT model from the arm being judged (same-model judging inflates BEAT via correlated errors as documented in irr-fidelity.md). BEAT criterion (pre-registered before run): panel win-rate > 0.5 with 95% binomial CI lower bound > 0.5 after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the full (arm x scaffold) family. This criterion is written to results/inference/preregistered_criteria.json by Phase 4 before Phase 5 executes.

ADJUDICATION MODEL INDEPENDENCE: Arm 1 (claude-sonnet skill) judged by claude-haiku-4-5. Arm 2a (haiku) judged by claude-sonnet-4-6. Arm 2b (sonnet) judged by claude-haiku-4-5. Arms 3-5 (pending) will use a non-matching model when keys available. Judge model recorded in every trial record.

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS: Family = all (arm x scaffold) combinations with at least one complete cell. BH correction applied to the binomial p-values for win-rate > 0.5. Power analysis (computed by power_analysis.py at workflow run-start) reports: given N=18 transcripts, k=3 replications, and panel size=3, power to detect win-rate delta=0.15 from 0.5. Pre-registered minimum power threshold: 0.80 (if actual power < 0.80 the report flags underpowered and recommends k increase before interpreting results).
