shuffle_seeds.py -- seeded RNG (seed=42 for reproducibility); for each S6 cell generate transcript utterance permutation; write shuffle_seeds.json keyed by cell_key; no random() calls at workflow runtime

run_cell.py -- provider-dispatch contract per grounding: idempotency check on cell_key.json; anthropic/openai SDK dispatch; utf-8+ensure_ascii=False everywhere; generous max_tokens; cost_log schema; artifact schema; DeepSeek json_object only with client-side validation; Qwen 2-pass thinking; Gemini version branch on thinkingBudget(int) vs thinkingLevel(str)

metrics.py -- Hungarian IDU alignment on utterance-set Jaccard (scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment); scipy.stats.kendalltau on matched (model_moment_rank, gold_moment_rank) pairs; adjacent-pair inversion rate; IDU count delta; Krippendorff alpha via irr.py alpha_nominal on aligned labels; schema_valid rate; grounding_integrity rate; write per-cell metrics JSONL; utf-8 throughout

power_analysis.py -- given N (transcripts), k (replications), panel_size (judges), delta (effect size from 0.5); compute binomial power for panel win-rate test; write power_report.json with recommendation if power < 0.80

report.py -- aggregate metrics_all.jsonl + band_calibration.json + adjudication/trials.jsonl; compute per-(arm,scaffold) match_rate, beat_rate, BH-corrected p-values; write per_cell_results.jsonl, match_beat_verdict.json, cost_frontier.json, summary.md with all required caveats
designs.token_estimate: Arm 1 cells: ~19 transcripts x 3 reps x 40k tokens = 2.3M tokens via agent() (claude-sonnet). Arm 2 cells: ~570 cells (haiku+sonnet x 5 scaffolds x 19 transcripts x 3 reps) x avg 12k tokens = 6.8M tokens via API (run_cell.py). Adjudication: ~90 judge calls x 3k tokens = 270k tokens. Orchestrators/harness agents: ~10 agents x 10k = 100k tokens. Total estimated: ~9.5M tokens. Note: Arm 2 tokens are API-side costs (billed), not workflow agent tokens; workflow agent token use (agent() calls) is dominated by Arm 1 (~2.3M) plus orchestrators (~100k) = ~2.4M workflow tokens.
designs.resumability: Every cell is idempotent: run_cell.py checks for existence of out_dir/cell_key.json (keyed by sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_stem)) before dispatching; if present, returns {status:skip, artifact_path:...}. Arm 1 skill cells: mpi_step.py manifest tracks substep status per run dir; a crashed run can be resumed by re-dispatching the agent which will skip already-closed substeps (status=done in manifest). Phase barriers in the workflow ensure phases 1-2 complete before phase 3 metrics run; phases 0 and 3-4 are single-agent checkpoints that can rerun idempotently (parse_gold.py and metrics.py overwrite only missing cell files). Phase 5 adjudication trials keyed by trial_id in trials.jsonl; already-judged trials are skipped. Arms 3-5 cells are enumerated but status=skip; when API keys are later provided, run_enumerate_cells.py again to flip their status and re-run the workflow -- existing arm 1-2 cells are not re-executed. The experiment_cells.json and shuffle_seeds.json written in Phase 0 are the authoritative cell registry and must not be regenerated mid-run (seeded shuffle reproducibility depends on this).
risks: Human-human ordering band estimated from n=1 transcript (p3s1 only). Applying it uniformly to 18 Phase-2 transcripts is a stated assumption, not a validated population estimate. Report must carry this caveat; MATCH verdicts are suggestive not definitive.

Phase-1 XLSX analyses (p1s1-p7s3) may have been seen by the LLM during plugin design (contamination risk). Phase-1 cells are labeled contamination_risk=true and excluded from primary verdicts; only Phase-2 held-out data drives the primary inference.

irr.py alignment mechanism has a known inversion bug (primary->alternate map used as alternate->primary lookup). Metrics.py uses deterministic Hungarian alignment instead, bypassing irr.py alignment entirely. If irr.py is patched mid-run, metrics.py must be re-run.

Same-model judging in Phase 5 inflates BEAT via correlated errors. Mitigated by judge-model independence rule (different model per arm) but cannot be fully eliminated for arm 2b (sonnet) if no non-Claude judge is available without an API key.

criteria_revision convergence loop (up to 5 passes) may cause arm 1 cells to timeout or vary substantially across replications. The orchestrator must handle status=flagged and re-dispatch; a cell that fails to converge in 5 passes is recorded as error and excluded from metrics.

Utterance numbering mismatch: kev's IRR CSV uses non-sequential utterance numbers (only participant turns numbered, not every Kevin Sheldrake turn). parse_gold.py and compute_band.py must reconcile utterance numbers against physical line order from the raw transcript file -- a line-counting reconciliation step is required.

Arms 3-5 (Gemini/DeepSeek/Qwen) are blocked on API keys and google-genai installation. The workflow produces a partial verdict without them; cost-quality frontier will be incomplete. Resumability design ensures backfill is possible.

transcript_prep register_offsets produces a flat-dict offset file (string utterance number keys); any change to offset format or utterance numbering between Phase 0 and Phase 1 will invalidate grounding checks at mpi_step.py close. Phase 0 must finalize transcript_prep before any arm 1 cells execute.

Power analysis may show underpowered design (k=3, N=18, panel=3 may not reach 0.80 power for delta=0.15). If power < 0.80 the workflow flags the result and recommends increasing k before interpreting match/beat verdicts.

Windows cp1252 default encoding will crash on Greek letters (alpha, kappa) and non-ASCII transcript content. All scripts must use open(..., encoding='utf-8') and json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False). Run-cell.py and metrics.py must encode this defensively.

fatal_flaws: cell_key = sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_stem) omits rep and seed. S6 is scheduled for 3 reps to measure shuffle variance, but reps 2 and 3 generate the same key as rep 1 and return `skip` immediately. The entire shuffle-variance signal is destroyed. The cell arithmetic admits the bug ('S6: 3 reps each = 57 + 38 = 95' cannot reconcile because 19 transcripts x 3 reps = 57 S6 cells, not 57+38). No within-cell variance estimate exists for any arm across any scaffold — single rep with Gemini forced to temp=1.0 leaves the benchmark unable to distinguish method variance from run noise.

The Phase 0 barrier test (reproduce_kappa) validates the IRR CSV path only (irr.py load_diachronic_csv on p3s1). Every tau-vs-gold value for all 39 transcripts runs through the XLSX parser (parse_gold.py/openpyxl) which is the central measurement tool of the entire benchmark. The XLSX parser is unvalidated by the headline barrier. A green reproduce_kappa tells you kev and yesesvi CSV loading works; it says nothing about whether parse_gold.py extracts the right moment integers, handles the misspelled sheet name, or preserves IDU order. The test_parse_gold_moment_not_rowindex unit test is listed but not part of the hard barrier — Phase 1 can proceed with a broken XLSX parser.

The Hungarian/Jaccard alignment compares two incompatible utterance numbering systems. The plugin's register_offsets assigns sequential integers to every physical line; the OSF gold (kev in XLSX and IRR CSVs) uses a non-sequential scheme numbering only participant-relevant turns with dotted/letter variants (22.1, 22a, 15a, 15). 'Utterance 8' in the plugin output and 'utterance 8' in the gold refer to different lines. The p3s1 transcript confirms: Kevin Sheldrake turns are multi-sentence, not one-utterance-per-line, so the plugin's sequential numbering diverges from kev's numbering from utterance 1 onward. Jaccard similarity on these sets approaches zero for all IDUs, making alignment random and every Kendall tau a noise value. The Phase 0 alignment test (kev-vs-yesesvi on p3s1) is within-OSF-numbering and manufactures false confidence — it validates alignment between two raters using the same base but tells you nothing about plugin-vs-gold alignment, which is the only path that matters in production.

BEAT is structurally unanswerable on the primary benchmark set (18 Phase 2 transcripts) and the adjudication mechanism is circular. Phase 2 has only one human rater (kev), so no human-human band exists and no beat threshold can be set — the design admits this with 'beat_candidate with caveat insufficient_irr_coverage_for_phase2.' The headline research question ('match or beat the human analyst') is unresolvable on the only uncontaminated data. The adjudication protocol for p3s1 asks a judge LLM to determine experienced-moment order from transcript text — identical epistemic access to what the analyst had. The judge cannot distinguish a better ordering from a differently-wrong one. The design's own 'verbal report != experience' caveat demotes adjudication from evidence to opinion, which it then uses to adjudicate claims. This is not a limitation to note — the beat half of the research question is unanswerable with this dataset.

The match criterion is statistically invalid and has near-zero discrimination power. The design tests whether model-vs-kev tau falls inside the human-human CI (computed over 6 IDU pairs from p3s1). This confounds two different quantities: the human-human agreement bound and the model-to-gold comparison. The correct test is an equivalence test (is model-vs-kev tau statistically indistinguishable from yesesvi-vs-kev tau?). With only 6 pairs, the bootstrap CI is extremely wide — nearly any tau value falls within it, making 'match=true' the default verdict regardless of model quality. Extrapolating this band uniformly to 18 transcripts with different structures and participant counts produces 18 unsupported verdicts. The core deliverable — 'match/beat verdict per method' — carries no statistical content for 18 of 19 transcripts.

Forced convergence on criteria_revision pass 2 is unimplementable without violating the doc-as-done contract. The design states force decision=converged 'via a modified prompt or direct manifest override.' A direct manifest override bypasses cmd_close, meaning no audit event and no git commit for that substep — verify's three-way join (manifest+audit+git) will flag the substep as inconsistent and block idu_naming_ordering. A modified prompt cannot guarantee convergence at the LLM level. The SKILL.md caps revision at 5 passes, but the design caps at 2 and forces after pass 2 — neither path is implemented in mpi_step.py, which only knows flagged/done. Arm 1 has a real deadlock: if criteria_revision returns more_revision_needed on pass 2, the cell either stalls indefinitely or violates the audit contract to escape. The 40 Arm-1 agents cannot be declared headless-runnable until this is resolved.
fixes: Add rep_index and shuffle_seed to the cell_key hash: sha256(model_id+scaffold_id+transcript_stem+str(rep_index)+str(shuffle_seed)). For non-S6 scaffolds, rep_index=0 and shuffle_seed=0 are constants. For S6, rep_index in {0,1,2} and shuffle_seed is the per-rep seed from precompute_shuffles.py. This makes reps genuinely distinct and idempotent across restarts.

Elevate parse_gold.py XLSX validation to the Phase 0 hard barrier. Add test_parse_gold_xlsx_p1s1 to the blocking pytest suite: recover p1s1.xlsx from git, run parse_gold.py, assert IDU count=9, assert moment integers match the Diachronic Structure sheet order, assert the misspelled sheet name 'Diachonic...' is handled. Gate phase 1 on this test alongside reproduce_kappa.

Build an explicit utterance numbering crosswalk before computing any tau. For p3s1: after recovering the kev IRR CSV and the raw transcript, map kev's utterance numbers to physical line positions by matching utterance text substrings. Verify the crosswalk on p3s1 (where both OSF numbers and plugin numbers are known) before trusting any Jaccard alignment. The test_hungarian_align_p3s1_pair unit test must use plugin-assigned utterance numbers, not OSF numbers, to be a valid pre-production test. If the crosswalk reveals systematic offset, apply it globally; if it reveals per-transcript variation, the alignment approach needs per-transcript calibration.

Replace the match verdict with a proper equivalence test or drop the quantitative verdict entirely. At n=6 pairs, report the point estimate tau_model_vs_kev and tau_hh alongside the raw alignment for human inspection. Explicitly state that no match/beat claim can be supported statistically from this data. The cost-quality frontier (cost vs tau) is still a valid deliverable; the match/beat binary is not.

Resolve the criteria_revision convergence contract before declaring Arm 1 headless-runnable. Options: (a) add a --force-converge flag to mpi_step.py close that accepts a flagged substep and re-closes it with decision=converged while preserving the close_id chain and emitting a forced_convergence audit event; (b) instruct the mpi-analyst to always return decision=converged after showing a revised grouping (hardcoded in the S1 scaffold prompt) accepting quality degradation in exchange for pipeline progress; (c) treat forced-convergence cells as a separate scaffold variant (S1-fc) and report tau separately. Do not allow silent manifest overwrites.

Preprocess the raw OSF transcripts to enforce the single-line-per-utterance invariant before running Arm 1. The p3s1 transcript shows Kevin Sheldrake turns spanning multiple sentences on one physical line. The plugin's register_offsets requires one utterance per line. Either define utterance boundaries consistently (e.g., one speaker turn = one utterance regardless of sentence count) and apply this to both transcript_prep and the gold crosswalk, or document that the plugin's utterance-numbering semantics differ from kev's and reflect this in all alignment and tau computations.
underspecified: The authoritative source for gold IDU ordering is ambiguous. Both the 'moment' column in the Diachronic Analysis sheet and the left-to-right IDU sequence in the Diachronic Structure sheet encode experienced order. The design uses the 'moment' column (parse_gold.py). These should agree, but if they disagree (e.g., a data entry error in the XLSX), which wins? The design does not specify a tiebreaker, and the Phase 0 unit test does not check for agreement between the two.

The Phase 2 coordinator's fan-out strategy for Arm 1 agents is stated as 'sequential for manifest contention' but the coordinator itself is a workflow agent subject to the ~16 concurrency cap and the 'keep structured returns small' constraint. It is unspecified how 40 sequential mpi-analyst agents are orchestrated without hitting workflow timeout limits. The coordinator's own token budget (5k) does not include the coordination overhead of 40 sequential agent dispatch-and-verify cycles.

The S2/S3/S4 scaffold prompts are sketched at the level of intent ('global timeline-first', 'forced permutation+justification') but their concrete prompt text — the actual messages sent to the Claude API via run_cell.py — is never specified. Phase 0 writes run_cell.py; but the scaffold prompt texts it dispatches are not written in Phase 0 and not written elsewhere. Phase 2 cells fire against undefined scaffold content.

The 'moment_label -> parse to temporal_position int' step in Phase 3 is unspecified. If the LLM returns a string like 'Moment Three' or a non-integer, the parsing fails silently or crashes. No schema-level enforcement of temporal_position as a positive integer exists in the current artifact schema (cell artifact has moment_label: str and temporal_position: int as stated, but run_cell.py's schema validation is not specified in detail).

The grounding_integrity metric is defined as 'fraction of IDUs with non-empty utterance_refs traceable to offsets registry.' For API-arm cells (Arm 2, scaffolds S2-S4), there is no offsets registry — register_offsets is an Arm 1 / mpi_step.py artifact. It is unspecified how grounding_integrity is computed for Arm 2 cells, or whether utterance_refs are even produced by the S2-S4 scaffold prompts.

The cost accounting for Arm 1 cells is listed as '40 Arm1 mpi-analyst agents x ~8k tokens' and explicitly noted as 'outside the workflow token budget.' The 8k estimate covers transcript_prep (3 substeps) + 3 diachronic substeps + up to 2 criteria_revision passes + schema_version-2 prompt artifacts for each LLM substep. A single idu_naming_ordering artifact with byte-accurate utterance_refs for 7-9 IDUs can exceed 4k tokens in the response alone, making 8k per cell likely 3-5x low for the diachronic-only token spend before orchestrator overhead.

The mpi-analyst.md description header says 'Receives a transcript plus few-shot examples' but the SKILL.md and zero-shot convention state no examples are injected. This contradiction leaves it unspecified whether Arm 1 cells are truly zero-shot or whether the mpi-analyst agent will attempt to load examples from examples/analyses/ (which the grounding notes is absent from this checkout) and fail or hallucinate.
salvage: Harness-first architecture is correct: writing and green-testing all deterministic Python tooling in Phase 0 before any agent cells fire is the right separation of concerns. The deterministic scripts (metrics, gold recovery, cell runner, shuffles) are independently testable and rerunnable outside any workflow.

File-keyed idempotent cells with small structured returns carrying only paths and status — long content stays in files — is the correct workflow pattern for resume safety and avoiding structured-return size limits.
Treating the OSF analyst (kev) as a rater rather than ground truth is methodologically honest and unusual enough to be a genuine contribution of the experimental design.

Precomputed seeded shuffles passed as CLI arguments to run_cell.py correctly respects the workflow runtime constraint that non-deterministic JS time/random calls are unavailable. This is the right way to handle S6 shuffle reproducibility.

Byte-offset grounding via utterance_refs as the basis for alignment (rather than fuzzy string matching) is the right instinct — the problem is not the approach but that the crosswalk from plugin line numbers to gold utterance numbers is not yet built.

The git/manifest verifier-fallback for Arm 1 resume ('orchestrator runs mpi_step.py verify, extracts artifact path from manifest if verify confirms done even if agent return is malformed') is a sound durable-side-effects-over-agent-returns pattern.

The blocked-arm skip/backfill design (run_cell.py returns status=skip reason=key_absent, idempotent backfill when keys arrive, no state reconciliation needed) correctly handles the reality that non-Claude API keys are absent without blocking the runnable cells or requiring workflow redesign when keys arrive.
Reporting Phase 1 results separately with a contamination flag rather than silently mixing them with Phase 2 results is correct experimental hygiene.

fatal_flaws: DEGENERATE HUMAN BAND — kappa vs ordering confusion: The design's match/beat criterion rests on a false empirical premise. kappa=0.82 measures utterance-to-IDU *assignment* agreement between kev and yesesvi, not IDU *ordering* agreement. When IDU-level Kendall tau is computed under the design's own alignment method (Hungarian on utterance-set Jaccard), tau=1.0 with bootstrap CI [1.0, 1.0] (n=6 IDU pairs, 2000 reps, seed=42) — both raters agree perfectly on moment order despite disagreeing on utterance boundaries. 'Match' therefore demands exact tau=1.0 (zero ordering errors tolerated); 'beat' demands tau>1.0 (mathematically impossible). Even the more generous utterance-level tau (n=~22 line pairs) gives CI upper bound of 1.0 by the same argument. The entire match/beat verdict framework is inoperable before a single model call is made.

WITHIN-LINE SPLIT BREAKS ALIGNMENT AND CAPS ACHIEVABLE TAU: Physical line 17 of p3s1.txt ('I was a bit surprised... My hands did move a bit as well') is assigned utterance numbers 15.1 (IDU 5, moment 5) and 15.2 (IDU 4, moment 4) in the gold CSV — one physical line, two IDUs, two different moments. Physical line 24 is split into 22.1/22.2/22.3. The plugin's one-line-one-canonical-number invariant means a model can assign line 17 at most one utterance number and one IDU. reconcile_utterances.py's exact-text matching cannot produce 1-to-many mappings; Hungarian alignment on utterance-set Jaccard will double-count line 17 as membership evidence for two gold IDUs simultaneously, corrupting the cost matrix. This is not a 'whitespace/coverage' reconciliation risk — it is a data-model incompatibility that structurally caps achievable tau below the required 1.0 for reasons entirely unrelated to model quality. A perfect model that perfectly replicates human analysis is graded as imperfect.

BEAT IS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION; ADJUDICATION SET EXPLODES: With upper CI bound = 1.0, no cell can ever achieve tau > upper, so the 'potential beat candidate' set is empty — Phase 3 never fires in the beat direction. The converse: any cell where the model makes even one IDU ordering error achieves tau < 1.0, which falls outside the [1.0,1.0] band, triggering Phase 3 adjudication. This means Phase 3 is not a rare exception path for close calls — it becomes the de facto verdict mechanism for the entire experiment. Since claude-sonnet-4-6 is both Arm2b producer and Phase 3 judge, the same-model circular adjudication flaw is not a corner case but the primary decision pathway.

IV CATEGORY LABELS WRONG FOR 4/7 BENCHMARK TRANSCRIPTS: Verified against actual transcript headers recovered from git history at d99e9f5. p8s1: design claims 'Low-IV', transcript header states 'Scored 4/5' (High). p10s1: design claims 'Moderate-IV', transcript header states 'Scored 4/5' (High). p12s1: design claims 'High-IV', transcript header states 'Scored 3/5' (Moderate). p1s2: design claims 'Moderate-IV', transcript header states 'Scored 4/5' (High). The benchmark does not cover all three IV strata as claimed; it covers only Moderate and High (if corrected labels are applied). The within-stratum comparison rationale collapses.

HEADLINE DELIVERABLE COLLAPSES TO 3 DATA POINTS AGAINST A DEGENERATE BAND: The design reports 231 cells, but demotes all non-p3s1 transcripts to 'distance-only, no verdict' because moment-ordering gold is unavailable in the markdown proxy (the markdown IDU table omits the Moment column — verified in convert_osf_analyses.py). Arm1 (the 'current implementation' headline arm) runs S1 only. The entire match/beat verdict reduces to p3s1 x Arm1-S1 x 3 reps = 3 data points, each individually compared against a band where the upper and lower bound are both 1.0. No statistical inference is possible. The stated deliverable — 'per-method match/beat verdict' — is not achievable as designed.

CIRCULAR ADJUDICATION — SAME MODEL AS PRODUCER AND JUDGE: claude-sonnet-4-6 is the Arm2b analysis producer and the Phase 3 adjudication judge for all contested cells. The random A/B label flip proposed in the design does not eliminate self-preference bias; it only makes the bias direction unknown, not absent. With Phase 3 being the primary verdict path (see above), this contaminates the primary outcome.
fixes: Replace the match/beat criterion entirely: abandon IDU-level tau on n=6 pairs as the comparison band. Either (a) collect ordering ratings from a third rater on multiple transcripts to get a distribution of human-human tau with non-degenerate variance, or (b) switch the primary metric to IDU count delta and IDU name edit-distance (already computable from existing artifacts), and treat tau as a secondary exploratory metric only. If tau is kept, report it as a continuous score without a match/beat threshold.

Resolve the within-line split mismatch before any alignment code is written: decide whether the pipeline unit is the physical transcript line or the analyst's sub-utterance. If the physical line is canonical, the gold CSV must be re-coded to one entry per physical line (merging 15.1+15.2 into one IDU or one moment entry). If the sub-utterance is canonical, the plugin must be extended to support sub-utterance numbering. The current position — gold uses sub-utterances, plugin uses physical lines, and reconcile_utterances.py bridges them via text-match — is technically unsound and must be explicitly resolved.

Fix IV category labels by reading transcript headers directly: use p9s2 (Low, scored 2/5) and p11s1 (Low, scored 2/5) for the Low stratum; retain p1s1 (High) and p3s1 (High) for the High stratum; pick an actual Moderate (scored 3/5) transcript — p12s1 is Moderate, not High as currently labeled. Rebalance the 7-transcript benchmark to genuinely span three strata before running.

To make non-p3s1 transcripts scoreable for ordering, recover the Moment column from raw XLSX files via git show d99e9f5 + openpyxl, mapping the Diachronic Analysis sheet column index (already known from convert_osf_analyses.py which parses `moment, idu_name, criteria = row[:6]`). Document the sheet-name and column-index contract in the harness so it is reproducible. Do not rely on the markdown proxy for ordering data.

Separate Phase 3 judge from Arm2b producer: use claude-opus-4 or claude-haiku-3-5 as Phase 3 adjudicator, or use a deterministic rule (higher tau wins; ties go to human analysts) rather than a model judge. If model judging is retained, log the full Phase 3 prompt so self-preference bias is detectable post hoc.

Add scipy as a declared harness dependency and implement kendalltau with p-value at the cell level. Compute tau on the Hungarian-aligned IDU pairs but also report n (number of pairs) alongside each tau so readers know the effective sample size. Flag cells where n < 4 as 'insufficient data, exclude from verdict'.
underspecified: Moment column recovery for non-p3s1 XLSX: the markdown proxy (examples/analyses/*.md) does not contain the Moment column — verified in convert_osf_analyses.py output format. The design assumes XLSX recovery from d99e9f5 via openpyxl, but does not specify the sheet name, the header row index, or the exact column mapping. Without this, distance-to-gold for non-p3s1 transcripts is uncomputable.

Arm2 prompt provenance and cross-arm comparability: the design says Arm2 reconstructs the 'S1 prompt extracted from SKILL.md.' The diachronic analysis prompt lives in agents/mpi-analyst.md and mpi-diachronic/SKILL.md jointly; the SKILL.md Closure section and agent tool declarations are part of the scaffold. If Arm2b's harness-injected prompt differs from what the Arm1 pipeline actually sends (e.g., missing the anti-fabrication guards, missing the transcript-span grounding requirement, missing the idu_naming_ordering JSON schema), the cross-arm comparison is confounded by prompt differences, not model differences.

reconcile_utterances.py exact-text matching strategy for sub-utterance lines: the design mentions text-match reconciliation but does not specify how a single physical line that maps to multiple gold utterance entries (22.1, 22.2, 22.3 from one physical line) is handled. The current description implies 1-to-1 mapping, which is impossible for lines that gold splits.

Grounding check definition for Arm2: the design mentions utterance-level grounding checks but does not specify whether these check (a) that the model's cited utterance number exists in the transcript, (b) that the quoted text matches the transcript at that line, or (c) both. The Arm1 pipeline enforces transcript-span grounding via the anti-fabrication schema; Arm2 must match this or the comparison is unfair.

Agent count / cost realism for full study: the design's agent-count estimate (~350 vs empirically-derived ~530) is unresolved. The cost estimate ($10-20 for Claude arms) is plausible for p3s1 only but does not account for the additional overhead if non-p3s1 XLSX parsing, reconcile_utterances.py development, and Phase 3 adjudication prompts are included.
salvage: Resumability and idempotency design is sound: sha256(model_id + scaffold_id + transcript_id + rep_number) as cell key with atomic JSON writes and seeded shuffles is the right architecture. Retain as-is.

Arm1 headless runnability is confirmed: the --allow-active-repo-nested flag is registered in mpi_step.py argparser and handled at line 243; global git identity (Test User / test@example.com) is set; hooks are disabled via core.hooksPath .git/hooks-disabled; GPG signing is disabled locally. Arm1 can run without modification.

Git recovery from d99e9f5 works cleanly: all OSF gold data (21 Phase 1 XLSX, 18 Phase 2 XLSX, 4 IRR CSVs, 18 Phase 2 transcripts, 42+36 markdown analyses) is recoverable via git show d99e9f5. The recovery mechanism is reliable for harness use.

Existing IRR pipeline reuse (alpha/kappa/ARI) is valid: irr.py's alpha_nominal, cohens_kappa, ARI, and bootstrap_ci functions are pure-stdlib, well-tested, and applicable to utterance-to-IDU assignment scoring without modification. Use these for the assignment-accuracy dimension of the benchmark rather than discarding the IRR infrastructure.

The descriptive distance-to-gold framing (IDU count delta, IDU name edit-distance, criteria overlap) is honest and achievable for all 39 transcripts without requiring ordering gold or a degenerate band. This is a viable alternative primary outcome that the design should promote from secondary to primary.

Phase 2 transcripts as held-out benchmark: 18 Phase 2 transcripts were not used during plugin development (plugin was calibrated on Phase 1). Using Phase 2 as the benchmark avoids any training-data contamination concern and provides a genuine held-out evaluation set. Retain this aspect of the design.

The underlying research question — whether a scaffolded LLM pipeline can replicate human MPI diachronic analysis at human-level inter-rater agreement — is scientifically interesting and answerable. The fatal flaws are all in the operationalization, not the research question. A redesigned experiment using IDU count delta + name edit-distance as the primary metric, with tau as exploratory, would be feasible and informative.

fatal_flaws: UTTERANCE-NUMBER SPACE MISMATCH INVALIDATES HEADLINE TAU. kev's gold CSV '#' column numbers all speakers sequentially across the interview (e.g., kev utt #8 = physical line 10, the 4th P3 turn). transcript_prep assigns sequential integers by physical line order (1-based, every line). These are different indexing schemes and are not aligned. Worse, kev splits single physical lines into sub-utterances (physical line 17 → kev #15.1 + #15.2; physical line 24 → kev #22.1, 22.2, 22.3), so there is no 1-to-1 mapping at all — a physical line can have two kev utterance numbers. The Hungarian-on-Jaccard alignment in metrics.py computes Jaccard overlap of model utterance_refs (transcript_prep line numbers) against gold utterance lists (kev's sequential-speaker numbers); these sets are disjoint by construction. Wrong IDU matching → wrong (model_moment, gold_moment) pairs → tau is garbage. The design mentions 'line-counting reconciliation' only for compute_band.py/parse_gold.py and never carries it into metrics.py's model-vs-gold alignment. Both arms are affected equally. There is no valid tau in this design as written.

ARM 2 IS NOT RUNNABLE: NO API KEY IN SUBPROCESS ENVIRONMENT. The design calls run_cell.py via Bash using anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=os.environ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY']). Verified: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent from all environment scopes (process env, Windows user-scope env, Windows machine-scope env, .env files). Claude is accessible only through the harness agent() primitive, not a raw key a subprocess can read. This kills 570 of 627 runnable cells (all arm-2a and arm-2b cells). The cost-logging and per-cell idempotency design for run_cell.py is also void. Arm 2 must route through agent() like arm 1, collapsing the cost-accounting scheme.

PSEUDOREPLICATION THROUGHOUT THE INFERENCE STACK. True independent n ≈ 6 participants (Phase 2: p8–p13). Three suggestions per participant share participant effects; k=3 replications per cell are not independent. The design pools all 18 transcripts × 3 reps into flat binomial CIs and applies BH-FDR correction assuming independence. Power is computed for N=18. The family for multiple comparisons is stated as all (arm × scaffold) combinations. None of these operations are valid under the actual correlation structure. MATCH/BEAT verdicts require clustered inference (cluster by participant at minimum). As written, precision is overstated by a large factor and the verdict is statistically unsound.

IDEMPOTENCY KEY OMITS REPLICATION SEED — COLLISION ACROSS ALL 3 REPS. cell_key = sha256(model_id + scaffold_id + transcript_stem) does not include the seed or rep index. All three reps of any cell hash to the same key. run_cell.py's skip-if-cell_key.json-exists logic will skip reps 2 and 3 after rep 1 completes, silently producing only k=1 per cell while the workflow believes k=3. The entire replication design is broken. The seed must be included in the idempotency key.

MATCH BAND IS CONCEPTUALLY PERVERSE, STATISTICALLY VOID, AND RESTS ON N=1. The symmetric interval [tau_HH - (1-tau_HH)/2, tau_HH + (1-tau_HH)/2] centered on a single p3s1 human-human tau penalizes a model that agrees with gold BETTER than yesesvi did (tau_model > upper bound → 'not matching'). The sensible 'treat gold as a rater' criterion is one-sided (tau_model_gold >= tau_HH), not symmetric. More fundamentally: tau_human_gold is undefined for the 18 Phase-2 primary transcripts — they each have only one human analyst (kev). Applying a band derived from a single Phase-1 transcript (p3s1, itself contamination-flagged) uniformly to held-out data is not a statistical test; it is a descriptive comparison against a reference line that has no sampling distribution. The design's own 'n=1, applied uniformly as stated assumption' language is a self-disqualifying flag — MATCH verdicts cannot be called verdicts.

BEAT ADJUDICATION PANEL IS CIRCULAR: SAME-MODEL-FAMILY JUDGES GRADING ORDERING COMPETENCE THEY THEMSELVES LACK INDEPENDENTLY. All runnable arms are judged by Claude Haiku or Claude Sonnet. These are the same model family (shared pretraining, RLHF, tokenizer) — exactly the 'correlated errors' phenomenon cited in irr-fidelity.md. The genuinely independent arms (Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen) are all skipped due to missing keys. Deeper: the research question is whether LLMs can distinguish experienced from narrative order; using an LLM judge to grade that capacity presupposes the judge has the competence under test. Candidate-BEAT selection ('model tau >= kev gold tau') also references a kev-vs-second-human tau that does not exist for Phase 2. The entire Phase 5 verdict mechanism is circular for all runnable arms.
fixes: UTTERANCE NUMBER RECONCILIATION MAP (prerequisite to any tau computation). Phase 0 must produce a reconciliation file for each transcript: a mapping from (transcript_prep physical-line utterance number) → (kev gold CSV '#' field) and vice versa. This requires: (a) recovering raw transcript, (b) recovering kev's CSV, (c) matching P3-speaker lines by content (fuzzy or exact substring match) allowing for the split-line case (one physical line → multiple kev sub-utterances). This map must be keyed by transcript stem and fed into both parse_gold.py and metrics.py before any alignment runs. Without this, all tau and Jaccard computations are invalid.

CHANGE IDEMPOTENCY KEY TO sha256(model_id + scaffold_id + transcript_stem + str(seed)). Update enumerate_cells.py, run_cell.py, and any existing cell_key.json files to include the rep seed. Rewrite experiment_cells.json after fixing the key function.

ROUTE ARM 2 THROUGH agent() OR EXPOSE KEY TO SUBPROCESS ENVIRONMENT. Either: (a) expose ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to the subprocess environment from the harness (requires confirming the harness key-injection mechanism), or (b) redesign arm 2 as agent() calls with model= parameter like arm 1, with cost logging via agent() token usage fields. Option (b) removes run_cell.py's per-cell cost logging but is immediately runnable. The design currently assumes both simultaneously (arm 2 described as 'direct API' but grounding says Claude arms run via agent()).

REPLACE SYMMETRIC MATCH BAND WITH ONE-SIDED DESCRIPTIVE BENCHMARK. Define match criterion as tau_model_gold >= tau_HH (kev-vs-yesesvi tau on p3s1) — a one-sided threshold, clearly labeled as descriptive against a single reference point, not a statistical test. Carry the n=1 caveat prominently in the report. Do not call this a 'verdict'; call it 'within human-human reference range' vs 'below human-human reference range'.

REPLACE BINOMIAL FLAT CIs WITH CLUSTERED INFERENCE. Use a mixed-effects or GEE model with participant as grouping factor (6 participants in Phase 2), or at minimum a permutation test that permutes at the participant level. The BH-FDR correction family should be the (arm x scaffold) combinations, but within-family observations must be clustered by participant before computing p-values. The k=3 reps should be averaged within each (transcript x cell) before entering the inference.

BEAT PANEL: USE GENUINE HUMAN JUDGES OR EXPLICIT OUT-OF-SCOPE DECLARATION. Given no non-Claude API keys are available, the Phase 5 panel cannot be genuinely model-independent. Either: (a) recruit human raters for the 6-transcript stratified sample (small; feasible), or (b) declare that BEAT verdict is deferred pending independent judge availability and report only the descriptive tau comparison. Remove the claim of BH-corrected BEAT verdicts from the abstract. Do not route haiku-vs-sonnet as 'model-independent'.
underspecified: RECONCILIATION BETWEEN kev's # COLUMN AND transcript_prep NUMBERING. The design mentions a 'line-counting reconciliation step is required' for compute_band.py but never specifies the algorithm, the output format, or how it propagates into metrics.py's Hungarian alignment. This is the most critical underspecification — the design cannot produce valid tau without it, and the specification of how to handle the split-line case (one physical line → two kev sub-utterances) is absent.

WHAT 'MOMENT NUMBER' MEANS IN MODEL OUTPUT FOR ORDERING COMPARISON. The mpi-analyst outputs moment as an integer assigned by the analyst (rule 7 in mpi-analyst.md: 'sequential integers starting from 1 reflecting experiential temporal order'). The gold moment numbers are kev's integers. The design treats these as directly comparable for Kendall tau, but it is never specified what to do when the model assigns different count of moments than gold — tau over matched pairs only (admitted in the design) creates different information content than tau over all pairs.

HOW THE WORKFLOW HANDLES criteria_revision CONVERGENCE ACROSS k=3 REPS IN THE SAME PHASE-1 AGENT. The design says each agent runs k=3 replications sequentially with convergence loop up to 5 passes. If a rep converges in pass 3 and another in pass 1, the agent's token budget varies dramatically. The design gives no mechanism for detecting or logging which rep required how many passes, and the 40k-token-per-transcript budget does not account for 5-pass worst-case on k=3 reps (15 diachronic LLM calls vs 9 assumed).

THE GOLD MOMENT-ORDER FOR PHASE-2 TRANSCRIPTS. The XLSX Diachronic Analysis sheet is stated as the source. parse_gold.py is specified to extract 'moment column from Diachronic Analysis sheet.' But convert_osf_analyses.py's mapping (which read these files) shows idu_counter is the sequential row index, not the moment column. The design says to use moment column for ordering, but does not specify what parse_gold.py does when multiple rows for the same IDU have different moment values (kev sometimes repeats moment numbers across IDU rows in the CSV), or how to handle missing/blank moment cells.

ZERO-SHOT ISOLATION ENFORCEMENT DURING arm-1 RUNS. mpi-analyst has the Read tool. The design recovers gold files to gold/<stem>_idus.json and osf-archive-recovered/ directories. No sandboxing, working-directory isolation, or file-permission restriction prevents an arm-1 agent from reading gold data during its run. The design states 'gold must NEVER enter analysis prompts' but provides no enforcement mechanism beyond agent instructions.

HOW power_analysis.py COMPUTES POWER FOR THE PANEL DESIGN. The function signature is given as power(N, k, panel_size, delta) for detecting win-rate delta from 0.5, but the computation is never specified. For a binomial panel test of win-rate > 0.5 the power depends on total trials, not just N and k independently. The pre-registration threshold (power >= 0.80) is stated but no formula is given for the binomial power calculation, and the design does not account for correlated judgments within the panel (3 judges on the same transcript are not independent).
salvage: Recovering gold from git d99e9f5 via 'git show' is correct and verified as the only available source for XLSX analyses and IRR CSVs.
Using the Moment COLUMN from the kev diachronic CSV (not the row-index idu_counter) as the gold experienced-order signal is the right choice and grounding-confirmed.
Dynamic experimenter-turn filter by Speaker column (rather than the hardcoded p3s1-specific set {10,21,...}) is the correct generalization for other transcripts.
Precomputing all shuffles and seeds in Phase 0 and writing shuffle_seeds.json before any cells execute correctly addresses the no-runtime-random constraint of the workflow journaling system.
Using 'python' not 'python3' and encoding='utf-8' / ensure_ascii=False throughout is verified correct for this environment (Python 3.13 on Windows with cp1252 default).

Phase 2 transcripts (p8s1-p13s3) as the held-out primary target with Phase 1 flagged as contamination_risk is the correct experimental hygiene choice given that Phase 1 XLSX analyses were used as plugin design fixtures.

Using deterministic Hungarian algorithm rather than irr.py's LLM alignment for IDU matching is the right instinct (irr.py alignment has a known inversion bug per irr-fidelity.md), even though the Jaccard input to Hungarian is broken by the numbering mismatch problem described in fatal_flaws.
Avoiding irr.py Kendall tau (it has none) and specifying a standalone metrics.py with scipy.stats.kendalltau is correct — scipy 1.17.1 is confirmed available under the 'python' binary.
The Phase 0 bootstrap structure (all scripts written, gold recovered, cells enumerated, seeds precomputed before any LLM cells execute) is the right sequencing for an idempotent resumable workflow.

Noting that the irr.py alignment inversion bug makes it unsuitable for metrics and routing around it is correct — the irr-fidelity design plan confirms the bug exists (alternate→primary map built as primary→alternate then used in the wrong direction).

ranking.name: Design 1 (Harness-First)
ranking.reason: Strongest BASE. The Phase-0-builds-and-unit-tests-everything-before-any-agent-fires barrier is the single most expensive asset to retrofit and is exactly the structure needed to test the crosswalk and XLSX parser before spending cells. Its idempotency/resumability and verifier-fallback patterns are sound. Weaknesses are all graftable: (a) cell_key omits rep+seed (its critique caught this, destroying S6 variance and silently collapsing k=3 to k=1); (b) it assumes run_cell.py dispatches Claude via os.environ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'] which does not exist on this machine -- ALL Claude arms must route through agent(); (c) its match verdict (tau in p3s1 band) is inoperable given the degeneracy I measured; (d) its Phase-0 barrier validates only the IRR CSV path, not the XLSX parser that scores all 39 transcripts. None of these touch the architecture, which is correct.

ranking.name: Design 3 (Statistician)
ranking.reason: The only statistically literate design and the source of the entire verdict layer to graft: pre-registered criteria written before cells run, power analysis, BH-FDR, explicit model-independent judge rule (different model family per arm), blind order-balanced adjudication, and the verbatim n=1 caveat. Loses to D1 on two graftable defects: (a) same broken subprocess-Claude architecture (run_cell.py with os.environ) -- dead given no keys; (b) its match band is SYMMETRIC, which is perverse -- it penalizes a model that agrees with kev BETTER than yesesvi did (treating gold as a rater demands a ONE-SIDED criterion). Its cell_key also omits the seed (critique caught the k=3->k=1 collapse). Its pseudoreplication is real (18 transcripts = 6 participants x 3) but its instinct toward clustered inference is closer to correct than the other two, which ignore clustering entirely.

ranking.name: Design 2 (Agent-Native)
ranking.reason: Best on two narrow axes: it is the only design with a rep-inclusive cell_key (sha256 includes rep_number) and the only one that scopes honestly (policy c: restrict match/beat to p3s1, treat Phase-2 as single-rater distance-to-gold). But it has verified FACTUAL errors -- IV category labels wrong for 4 of 7 benchmark transcripts (claimed Low/Moderate where transcript headers say High) -- which means its stratified-comparison rationale collapses. It is blind to the band degeneracy, and its Phase 3 adjudication is circular (claude-sonnet is both Arm2b producer and judge). The agent-native pattern (each cell an agent, verifier after) is more expensive per cell than D1's thin-wrapper-over-tested-scripts and provides no offsetting benefit here. Salvage its cell_key and scoping; discard the rest.

adjudication.merge_prescription:
BASE = Design 1's harness-first skeleton: Phase 0 writes AND green-unit-tests every deterministic Python script (gold_recovery, parse_gold, crosswalk, metrics, run_cell-external-only, precompute_shuffles) behind a hard barrier; no agent cell fires until all tests pass. Phases 1-N are thin agent/Bash wrappers over those scripts.

GRAFT FROM DESIGN 3 (the entire inference/verdict layer): (1) pre-registered criteria file written to disk BEFORE any scoring cell runs; (2) power_analysis.py executed at run-start with a flag if power<0.80; (3) participant-clustered inference -- average k reps within each cell, then cluster by participant (n=6 in Phase 2), BH-FDR across the arm x scaffold family; (4) the model-independent judge rule (judge model must be a DIFFERENT family than the arm judged) and blind, order-balanced adjudication; (5) the verbatim n=1 band caveat in the report.

GRAFT FROM DESIGN 2: (1) policy-(c) scoping -- match/beat verdict restricted to p3s1; Phase-2 transcripts reported as single-rater descriptive distance-to-gold, never a verdict; (2) the rep-inclusive cell_key instinct.

MANDATORY FIXES (blocking; drafter must implement all):
(F1) cell_key = sha256(model_id + scaffold_id + transcript_stem + str(rep_index) + str(seed)). D1 and D3 both omit rep/seed -> silent collapse of k=3 to k=1. Non-degenerate.
(F2) ALL Claude arms (Arm1 skill + Arm2 Haiku/Sonnet tiers) route through the workflow agent() primitive, NOT run_cell.py-with-os.environ. No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exists in any scope on this machine. run_cell.py is for EXTERNAL providers only and stays dead until the user supplies keys. Cost accounting for Claude arms comes from agent() token-usage fields.
(F3) Build a utterance-numbering CROSSWALK in Phase 0 and elevate it -- together with the XLSX parser test and reproduce_kappa -- to the HARD barrier, BEFORE any tau is computed. The crosswalk maps transcript_prep physical-line numbers <-> kev's gold sub-utterance numbers. It MUST handle the 1-to-many split-line case (physical line 17 -> kev 15.1 + 15.2 at DIFFERENT moments; line 24 -> 22.1/22.2/22.3). Record per-transcript coverage %; if coverage <80%, drop that transcript from any verdict. Without this, every Hungarian-on-Jaccard alignment in all three designs is noise (the two numbering spaces are disjoint by construction).
(F4) The PRIMARY metric is chosen by the Phase-0 band computation, not assumed. I ran it: kev vs yesesvi moment ordering on p3s1 is tau=1.0 at both utterance (n=16 shared) and IDU (6 pairs) level, robust to the recode. The band is DEGENERATE. Therefore tau-vs-a-band CANNOT be the headline verdict. Make IDU-count-delta and IDU-name edit-distance the PRIMARY descriptive metrics (computable for all 39 transcripts without ordering gold); report tau as a secondary continuous score with NO match/beat threshold derived from the p3s1 band.
(F5) criteria_revision forced-convergence must use a real mpi_step.py --force-converge flag that re-closes the flagged substep preserving the close_id chain and emitting a forced_convergence audit event, OR a hardcoded-converge S1 scaffold variant reported separately. NEVER a direct manifest override -- that breaks verify's three-way manifest+audit+git join and blocks idu_naming_ordering.
(F6) Sandbox the Arm1 run dir / working directory so the Read-tooled mpi-analyst agent cannot read recovered gold (gold/, osf-archive-recovered/) mid-run. Zero-shot isolation must be structurally enforced, not just instructed.
adjudication.verdict_criteria:
PHASE-0 BRANCH (already resolved by measurement): kev-vs-yesesvi moment-ordering tau on p3s1 = 1.0 (utterance-level n=16; IDU-level n=6; robust to recode). The human-human ORDERING band is DEGENERATE -- the raters disagree on utterance->IDU boundaries (kappa=0.82) but NOT on moment order. Consequence the final workflow MUST encode:

(1) NO tau-within-band match verdict. A symmetric or band-based tau criterion is mathematically inoperable here: 'match' would demand tau=1.0 exactly and 'beat' would demand tau>1.0 (impossible). Designs 1, 2, and 3 all anchor on this and all fail.

(2) MATCH (p3s1 only, ONE-SIDED, human-fallibility-aware): an arm MATCHES iff its agreement with the kev gold is >= the kev-vs-yesesvi human-human agreement, within sampling error, on the SAME metric. Because the ordering band is degenerate (1.0), the operative match dimension is utterance->IDU ASSIGNMENT agreement (Krippendorff alpha / Cohen kappa via irr.py, where the human band is the real kappa=0.82, NOT 1.0), plus IDU-count-delta and IDU-name edit-distance. One-sided because gold is a RATER: agreeing with kev as well as or better than yesesvi did = match-or-better, never 'out of band.' Ordering tau is reported as a descriptive continuous score, flagged 'human band degenerate (tau=1.0); no discriminating ordering threshold available from p3s1.'

(3) PHASE-2 (18 transcripts, single rater kev): NO match/beat verdict. Report IDU-count-delta, IDU-name edit-distance, and tau-vs-kev as descriptive distance-to-gold, explicitly labeled 'single-rater reference, no human-human band.'

(4) INFERENCE: average k reps within each cell; cluster by participant (n=6 in Phase 2 -- the 18 transcripts are 6 participants x 3 suggestions, NOT 18 independent units); apply BH-FDR across the arm x scaffold family; flag 'underpowered' if power<0.80; carry the n=1 band caveat verbatim.

(5) BEAT: NOT claimable in the no-external-key configuration. All runnable arms are Claude (Haiku/Sonnet); a Claude judge grading Claude producers yields correlated errors (the irr-fidelity 'same-family' failure). BEAT requires a model-independent judge (different family) OR human raters. In the current config, report BEAT as 'DEFERRED -- pending independent adjudication.' When an independent judge exists: blind, order-balanced presentation, >=3 judges, majority vote per disputed pair, win-rate>0.5 with binomial CI lower bound >0.5 after BH-FDR, pre-registered before cells run. Mandatory caveat on every adjudication record: the transcript records VERBAL REPORT, not experience; a judge cannot distinguish a 'better' ordering from a 'differently-wrong' one, so beat verdicts carry irreducible uncertainty.

decision_points_for_user.question: External (non-Claude) API keys -- Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen -- are absent everywhere on this machine. How many should be provisioned before the run?
options: None (Claude arms only -- Arm1 skill + Haiku/Sonnet tiers)
One cheap key (OpenRouter or DeepSeek key-only, no install) for a single non-Claude arm
All three (requires GEMINI_API_KEY + pip install google-genai, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, DASHSCOPE_or_OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
decision_points_for_user.recommendation: Provision at least one non-Claude key (DeepSeek or OpenRouter is lowest-friction -- the openai SDK 2.31.0 is already installed, key-only). This unblocks the cross-model comparison arms AND -- critically -- provides the ONLY non-circular path to a BEAT verdict, since a different-family model can judge Claude producers without correlated-error contamination. Without any external key, BEAT stays out of scope.

decision_points_for_user.question: The human-human ordering band exists only on p3s1 (the single IRR transcript) and is degenerate (tau=1.0). Should a blind second human rater code a subset of Phase-2 transcripts to establish a real, non-degenerate band?
options: No second rater (band stays n=1 and degenerate; Phase-2 stays single-rater descriptive)
Second human rater on 3-6 Phase-2 transcripts (1-2 per IV stratum)
Second rater on the full Phase-2 set (18 transcripts)
decision_points_for_user.recommendation: Offer the 3-6 transcript option. It is the ONLY way to obtain a non-degenerate human-human band beyond p3s1 and the only way to make MATCH a real statistical test (and BEAT meaningful) on held-out data. Without it, the headline match/beat claim is confined to p3s1's assignment-agreement dimension and Phase-2 remains descriptive only. Even a small second-rater sample changes the deliverable from 'descriptive comparison' to 'statistical verdict.'

decision_points_for_user.question: What is the token/cost budget cap for the run?
options: Calibration-only: p3s1 + a few Phase-2 transcripts, k=3 (cheapest, validates the harness end-to-end)
Full Phase-2 held-out benchmark, k=3 (the primary deliverable)
Full Phase-2 + Phase-1 contamination-flagged sanity set
decision_points_for_user.recommendation: Run phased: calibration-only first to green the harness and confirm the crosswalk coverage is >=80% per transcript, THEN full Phase-2. Phase-1 is contamination-flagged (its XLSX analyses were plugin design fixtures) so add it only as a clearly-separated sanity comparison, never mixed into the primary verdict. This bounds spend while surfacing the crosswalk-coverage risk before the expensive full run.

decision_points_for_user.question: How many judges in the adjudication panel for BEAT?
decision_points_for_user.recommendation: 3 judges (majority vote per disputed pair) -- but this decision is MOOT until decision point 1 is resolved, because no independent (non-Claude-family) judge exists without an external key, and same-family judging is disqualified by correlated-error bias. If only Claude is available, the panel question does not arise: BEAT is deferred, not run.
